The deceased was identified as Al-Amin, 35, of Baripota village under Nabharan union.

The incident took place around 10:30pm in Baripota village.

According to police and local residents, Al-Amin was on his way home after Taraweeh prayers when a group of miscreants attacked him. The attackers stabbed him with sharp weapons indiscriminately, leaving him critically injured, and fled the scene.

Locals rescued him in a bloodied condition and rushed him to Sharsha Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared him dead.

Confirming the incident, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sharsha Police Station, Maruf Hasan said he is currently on leave, and the inspector (investigation) is looking into the matter.

Inspector (Investigation) Shah Alam of the same police station said police have already started working to identify the motive behind the murder and those involved.

“The body has been sent to Jashore General Hospital for an autopsy,” he added.
summary: Police started working to identify the motive behind the murder, says Inspector Sharsha

The group has been earning more than Tk 1 crore per month from the illicit activities, CID Special Superintendent Jasim Uddin Khan said today.

CID officials said the arrestees had long been involved in an organised syndicate engaged in unauthorised NID corrections, insertion of fake information, and the illegal sale of citizens’ personal data.

Photo: Collected Police have arrested a youth in connection with an attempt to attack Abdullah Al Amin, a candidate of the National Citizen Party (NCP) for the Narayanganj-4 constituency.

The youth was arrested around 3:00am today after he initially fled from the scene, confirmed Anowar Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Fatullah Model Police Station.

The arrestee has been identified as Al Amin alias "Akka-Bakka Alamin", 24, of Gaibandha Sadar. He had been living in a rented house in Bashmuli area of Poshchim Deobhog under Kashipur union, from where he was arrested.

Meanwhile, in a press release, Rab-11 said, they have arrested the prime suspect, Maruf Hasan, in connection with the attempted attack on the NCP leader during a special drive in the Char Kashipur area around 2:00am. According to Rab-11 Deputy Director Abdur Rashid, investigation showed that Maruf was accompanying Al Amin during the incident; when suspicion was raised towards Al Amin, he fled the scene.

Maruf, 22, is the son of late Ayub Ali of Char Kashipur, the statement said.

Rab-11 Deputy Director Abdur Rashid also said the suspect has been handed over to Fatullah Police Station.

The incident took place around 7:30pm yesterday, during a door-to-door campaign on referendum. At least two NCP activists were injured during a scuffle, said candidate Abdullah Al Amin, who is also the party’s joint member secretary.

Speaking to The Daily Star over the phone, Abdullah said he was campaigning with around 40 to 50 party activists, interacting with local residents while walking through the area.

“At one point, we noticed a young man following us. On suspicion, we stopped and searched him and found a machete hidden inside his clothes,” he said.

Asked why he was carrying the weapon, the youth claimed that someone has instructed him to follow them with it, Abdullah added.

Describing the area as a hub for drug dealers and juvenile gang members, he said more people quickly gathered at the spot, and taking advantage of the situation, the armed man managed to flee.

“Local residents then advised me to leave the area immediately, and I was safely taken away in a vehicle,” he said.

A general diary has been filed with the Fatullah Police Station today, where Abdullah mentioned previously receiving threats over phone.
summary: General diary filed with the Fatullah Police Station

Photo: Collected A nine-year-old girl from Cox’s Bazar, who was struck by a stray bullet fired from Myanmar on Sunday, has been placed on life support at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital (NINS) in Dhaka.

"Her condition is still very critical, and she is under observation at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU)," Humayun Kabir Himu, an associate professor at NINS, and her uncle, Shawkat Ali, told The Daily Star today.

Huzaifa Afnan, a class-3 student from the Teschi Bridge area of Whykong union, was shot during intense clashes between the Arakan Army and Rohingya armed groups inside Myanmar.

She was rushed to Chattogram Medical College Hospital and later shifted to NINS last night after doctors at CMCH failed to remove the bullet lodged in her throat.

Humayun said the bullet remained stuck in her throat, but she suffered a stroke as it damaged the veins that supply blood to the brain.

This also increased pressure on her brain, and she was put on mechanical ventilation (life support), he said, adding that she had been given medication to reduce the pressure.

She is very young and is showing some response -- two positive signs -- but nothing can be said for certain at this stage, Humayun said. The next procedure may be carried out once the pressure on her brain eases, he added.

A board led by NINS Director Prof Kazi Gias Uddin Ahmed is overseeing her treatment. No decision has yet been taken about sending her abroad for better treatment.
summary: Doctor says bullet lodged in throat caused stroke

The incident took place in Mahendranagar area of Sadar upazila while she was walking from Lalmonirhat town towards Kurigram. Following the incident, Detective Branch (DB) of police and Sadar thana police conducted a joint operation and arrested a young man accused in the case.

The victim filed a case at Lalmonirhat Sadar Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. Lalmonirhat DB Officer-in-Charge Saad Ahmed confirmed the incident yesterday.

The arrested man has been identified as Abu Kalam, 31, of Kashipur village under Mahendranagar union.

According to police, the female tourist had been travelling on foot across different districts of the country for the past month. After arriving in Lalmonirhat, she visited several tourist spots in the district. Later, she set out on foot for Kurigram on the morning of January 11.

When she reached Mahendranagar area, about six kilometres from Lalmonirhat town, she needed to use a toilet. At that time, she went to a roadside house and sought permission to use the toilet. While returning from the toilet, Abu Kalam, a resident of the house, allegedly harassed her and attempted to outrage her modesty.

When the victim screamed, other members of the household rushed to the spot. However, instead of seeking justice, they allegedly tried to assault her by accusing her of theft. Somehow, the female tourist managed to leave the house and went live on Facebook, tearfully describing the entire incident. The video went viral on social media within moments.

In the Facebook live video, the female tourist said, “I set out to travel the country on foot one month ago. Before coming to Lalmonirhat, I visited many districts. I did not face any problems anywhere. But after coming to Lalmonirhat, I had to face such an unpleasant situation.”

She further said, “It is very painful to think about our social system. I was harassed and sought justice, but instead, an attempt was made to label me a thief.”

Yesterday afternoon, the victim told journalists that after watching her Facebook live video, DB police quickly arranged for her security.

“I do not know the accused man. But the police identified him within a short time and arrested him,” she said.

OC Saad said, “After watching the Facebook live video, we took immediate action. After the incident, the accused fled his house. Later, with the help of the local police, he was arrested.”

He added that the victim is now in a stable condition and has once again set out to travel the country on foot.
summary: Lalmonirhat DB arrests the suspect after victim’s Facebook live video goes viral

title: Arson attacks on minorities’ homes in Ctg: Six more held
body:
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() { // Share dropdown toggle const shareToggle = document.querySelector('.share-toggle'); const shareMenu = document.querySelector('.share-menu'); if (shareToggle && shareMenu) { shareToggle.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); shareMenu.classList.toggle('hidden'); }); // Close dropdown when clicking outside document.addEventListener('click', function() { shareMenu.classList.add('hidden'); }); shareMenu.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); } // Copy link functionality const copyBtn = document.querySelector('.copy-link-btn'); if (copyBtn) { copyBtn.addEventListener('click', function() { const url = this.getAttribute('data-url'); navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function() { // Show success message const originalText = copyBtn.innerHTML; copyBtn.innerHTML = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(function() { copyBtn.innerHTML = originalText; }, 2000); }); }); } }); Staff Correspondent, Ctg A series of arson attacks in Raozan and Rangunia upazilas of Chattogram were carried out in a planned manner to embarrass Bangladesh internationally ahead of the national election, Chattogram district police claimed yesterday.

According to police, the attackers set fire to the homes of members of the Hindu, Buddhist and hill communities. The same group had also planned to torch educational institutions ahead of the election to draw greater media attention.

Police yesterday arrested six more people in connection with the arson attacks on residential houses. Chattogram Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Ahsan Habib Palash disclosed the information at a press conference at the Chattogram District Police office following the arrests.

With the latest arrests, a total of seven people have been detained so far in connection with the incidents. Police said a group of around 16 to 17 members was involved at different stages of the attacks.

Police also seized various materials used in the arson attacks, along with a CNG-run auto-rickshaw and a motorcycle.

The arrestees were identified as Mohammad Omar Faruk, Mohammad Kabir Hossain, Kartik De, Biplab Barua, Mohammad Lokman and Md Parvez. Earlier, police arrested another individual named Monir.

Speaking at the press conference, DIG Palash said, “Many of those who have been arrested are members of a banned organisation. They believed that by creating an embarrassing situation in the country, many of their leaders would get an opportunity to return to the country and a favourable environment would be created for them.”

However, the DIG did not disclose the name of the banned organisation.

“We have identified one individual who is the mastermind and played an active leadership role in the incidents. He is involved in the local nursery business. We have obtained the names of several others and we are trying to arrest them. A former commissioner affiliated with the banned organisation provided financial support to those involved in implementing the plan,” the police official said.

DIG Palash further said, “The arson attacks were carried out to prove that communal harmony does not exist in Bangladesh and that Hindu, Buddhist and hill communities are not safe here, so that Bangladesh would be embarrassed internationally. The intention was to make the upcoming national election questionable -- if these communities are portrayed as unsafe, it would be claimed that a proper election environment does not exist.

“Initially, the incidents did not receive the level of attention the attackers had expected. As a result, the pace of their activities gradually increased, and in the last couple of incidents, entire houses were completely gutted in arson attacks. From interrogation so far, we have learned that they prepared a plot to set fire to educational institutions to attract greater media attention."

“No specific community was targeted under this arson ‘package’ -- Hindus, Muslims and Buddhists were all among the victims. Through these incidents, an attempt was made to create communal tension inside the country and, on the other hand, to spread propaganda about minority persecution in Bangladesh to mislead the international community and put the government in an awkward position,” he added.

Police said investigations are ongoing to identify others involved in the incidents.

In December last year, several arson attacks took place in Raozan and Rangunia late at night after doors were locked from the outside. Police also recovered several handwritten banners from areas adjacent to the crime scenes. However, no casualties were reported.
summary: Police claim attacks aimed to create communal tension and undermine election credibility

Alcohol, yaba and cannabis were seized from the house that belonged to Abdullah Al Jahir, an additional deputy inspector general of police.

Jahir had rented out the house, where drug use and illegal “DJ parties” had allegedly been going on for a long time, prompting police to conduct the raid, Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (detective) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told The Daily Star.

Parties and drug consumption were regularly reported at the property in Police Housing-1, said Elias Kabir, deputy commissioner of DB’s Uttara division that conducted the raid.

Jahir was the primary organiser of the parties and a man named Mahbub Alam acted as the co-organiser, according to Elias.

Mahbub told investigators that Jahir received 70 percent of the earnings from the parties, while he took the rest, according to DB. The property was available for bookings through Airbnb, and “DJ parties” were regularly organised for those who booked it.

The arrestees have been sent for summary trial, Elias said.

Meanwhile, following the incident, Jahir, an officer from the 24th police batch, has been attached to the Police Headquarters.

Speaking to The Daily Star, Jahir said that his house had facilities for hosting birthday parties and family gatherings.

They take bookings through Airbnb, but drugs and “DJ parties” are prohibited under their rules. Those who violated the restrictions were blacklisted and fined, he said.

Regarding Monday night’s incident, Jahir said the property had been rented out for a birthday party, but the guests brought drugs, which were recovered during the DB raid.

“What is our crime here? We rented out the property. Our guidelines explicitly prohibit drugs and DJ parties. Those found with drugs committed criminal offences,” he said, while dismissing allegations that such parties were organised every day.

Every month, two to three parties were held at the venue, Jahir added.

Meanwhile, Opposition Leader and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman has expressed concern over the country’s deteriorating law and order situation following the recovery of drugs and arrests.

The involvement of a property belonging to a senior police official in such an incident has created concern and fear among the public, he said in a Facebook post.

The incident itself reflected the extent of the deterioration in law and order across the country.

Extortion, snatching, looting, robbery and other criminal and anti-social activities had reached alarming levels, he said.

An SRB-5 team received information around 2:00am that a suspicious cement sack had been left on the eastern side of a litchi orchard in Aduburi, Lt Col Md Faisal Ishtiaq, commanding officer of SRB-5, told The Daily Star.

Acting on the information, the team conducted a drive and recovered the crude bombs from the sack in the presence of witnesses, he said.

Of the bombs, 64 were wrapped in red cellophane tape and 39 in black cellophane tape, he added.

The recovered items were later handed over to Kashiadanga Police Station through a general diary entry for legal action, he said.

An investigation is underway, and legal action will be taken against those involved, the SRB official added.

Photo: Forest Department Trees are allegedly being felled and uprooted in a reserved forest at Char Signboard in Patuakhali’s Rangabali upazila to make way for watermelon cultivation, with an excavator being used to build an embankment.

The Forest Department has filed two cases and lodged a GD with police over the alleged destruction. However, attempts to occupy the land have reportedly continued, with forest officials alleging obstruction and threats.

The dispute centres on a two-year lease of 30 acres within the reserved forest. The Forest Department has twice asked the district administration to cancel it, saying the land falls within a protected forest area.

According to Forest Department sources, 415 acres at Char Signboard were declared a reserved forest on April 4, 2010. Mangrove species were planted there, including jhau trees on 10 hectares during the 2021-22 fiscal year.

Photo: Forest Department Amir Hossain, ranger of Rangabali Range, said the district administration leased out 30 acres in the area last year. He alleged that leaseholders Arif Mir and Manik Molla cut trees from a jhau plantation to prepare the land for watermelon cultivation.

The two cases are pending in court. Despite this, work to build an embankment using an excavator began on October 17, allegedly under Arif Mir’s leadership, he said.

“After receiving reports that 200-300 chaila, keora and jhau trees had been uprooted, forest officials tried to stop the work, but it continued despite their objections.”

The department lodged a GD with Rangabali Police Station on October 17, naming three people, including Arif Mir, said the ranger, adding that forest officials had faced obstruction before and that staff shortages often forced them to retreat.

Contacted, Arif Mir denied attempting to grab forest land.

“We have taken a government lease of the land,” he said, but declined to show the lease document or disclose how much he had paid.

This correspondent obtained a permission document issued to 25 farmers by the Rangabali upazila land office on October 13, 2025, bearing the signature of the then upazila nirbahi officer (UNO).

The document allowed cultivation for one season or one year and stated that it could not be used as an official government document in court. It did not identify the issuing official or specify the issuance date or revenue collected.

In a letter dated October 15, Divisional Forest Officer Mohammad Zahidur Rahman Mia urged the deputy commissioner to cancel the lease, warning that it could threaten the forest, wildlife, biodiversity and surrounding mangrove ecosystem.

Rangabali UNO Nazmul Hasan said no such permission had been granted since he took office.

“I do not know how the land was leased out. However, an initiative has been taken to identify forest land and khas land in consultation with the forest department and the leaseholders,” he said, adding that action would be taken if anyone had cut trees.

Abdul Qaiyum, additional deputy commissioner (revenue) of Patuakhali, said the administration was examining the forest department’s letter.

“We are verifying the information and will take action in accordance with the rules. We will also investigate whether there were any irregularities in granting permission for cultivation in the past,” he said.

Photo: Collected A woman has been accused of beating her neighbour’s cat to death in Chakaria upazila of Cox’s Bazar.

The cat’s owner, Shamsul Alam, 54, filed a written complaint with Chakaria Police Station yesterday, seeking justice.

Shamsul Alam, a resident of Kazirpara in Chakaria municipality, went to the police station yesterday afternoon with the cat’s body in a cage and filed the complaint.

According to the complaint, Shamsul Alam chased the dog of his neighbour, Firoza Begum, when it tried to attack two of his cats yesterday morning.

Enraged, Firoza beat the cat to death with a stick, Shamsul alleged in the complaint.

He said he had raised the cats with great care and wanted justice for the incident.

Chakaria Police Station Officer-in-Charge Arifur Rahman said killing an animal is a punishable offence. Police would investigate the complaint and take legal action accordingly.

The other three bodies were recovered in Jhenaidah, Kurigram and Rangpur.

Police recovered the decomposed body of an unidentified man, aged around 35-40, from a pond at Shah Makhdum Institute Public Library in Rajshahi city this morning.

The body was recovered around 9:00am following information from local residents, said Md Gaziur Rahman, spokesperson for Rajshahi Metropolitan Police (RMP).

He said the man might have died two to three days ago, possibly by drowning or due to other causes. His identity could not be established immediately as decomposition had disfigured his face and body.

A 35-year-old man was allegedly hacked to death with an axe by his father-in-law while sleeping at his in-laws’ house in Bolibhadrpur village of Maheshpur upazila around 6:30am today.

The deceased was identified as Golam Rahman alias Abdur Rahman.

Locals detained Golam’s father-in-law Tarikul Islam, 45, after he allegedly walked around carrying the axe following the killing, and handed him over to police. The victim’s wife was also taken to the police station for questioning.

According to local sources, Golam married Tarikul’s eldest daughter, Hazera Khatun, two years ago. As Hazera was staying at her parents’ home, Golam visited his in-laws last night. The following morning, Tarikul allegedly attacked him with an axe while he was asleep.

Abdus Sattar, a former union parishad member, said Tarikul had a history of mental health problems and had previously been kept in a psychiatric institution.

Maheshpur Police Station OC Imran Alam said there had been longstanding tensions between the two men over family disputes. Police recovered the body and the axe allegedly used in the killing. The motive remains under investigation.

Police recovered the body of Moksed Ali alias Bachchu Mia, 61, with his throat slit from a bedroom at his nephew’s house in Panditpara area under Dharanibari union in Ulipur upazila early today.

Bachchu Mia, a resident of Rangpur city, had come to visit his village home and was staying at his nephew Mithu Mia’s house. Police received information about the murder through the national emergency service around 2:20am. The victim’s elder sister, Mazeda Begum, identified the body.

Ulipur Police Station OC Shawkat Ali said police had prepared an inquest report and sent the body to Kurigram General Hospital morgue for autopsy. The motive and those responsible remained unknown, and no arrests had been made as of this morning.

The process of filing a case and taking further legal action was underway.

Fakhrul Alam Ratan, 50, a member of the Balapara Union Awami League, was attacked by several assailants wielding sharp weapons on a road in front of his home in Haricharan Laskar village of Kaunia upazila yesterday afternoon.

According to police, quoting relatives and eyewitnesses, the attackers surrounded Ratan and hacked him indiscriminately before fleeing. Local residents rescued him and took him to hospital, where a doctor declared him dead.

Ratan had previously worked for a non-governmental organisation but later left the job to look after his land and property.

Nazrul Islam, organising secretary of the Balapara Union Awami League unit, said Ratan was a member of the union unit.

Kaunia Police Station OC Badal Kumar Mondal said police were investigating whether the killing stemmed from previous enmity or another dispute. The attackers had not been identified and no case had been filed, he added.

Police recovered the decomposed body of an unidentified man, believed to be around 50, from the bank of Turag river in Protyasha Math area of Tongi last night.

Firoz Uddin, officer-in-charge of Tongi River Police Station, confirmed the recovery today.

He said local residents spotted the body on the riverbank in the area under Tongi West Police Station and informed police. River police later went to the scene and recovered it.

Tongi West Police Station OC Md Arifur Rahman said the body showed signs of decomposition. An unnatural death case has been filed, and the body is being kept at the morgue of Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College for autopsy.

Our correspondents from Lalmonirhat, Rajshahi, Jhenaidah and Gazipur contributed to this report.

Photo: Collected A key suspect in the murder of journalist Lutfuzzaman Fakir alias Alif Fakir was arrested in Durgapur upazila of Netrokona, the Special Response Battalion (SRB) said.

Ashikur Rahman Prangon, 21, was arrested during a special drive in the Shaheed Minar area of Durgapur municipality around 11:45pm yesterday.

Abul Hasan, additional superintendent of police and senior assistant director of the media wing of SRB-14, Mymensingh, confirmed the arrest today.

“Everything cannot be disclosed in the interest of the investigation. However, considering the technical aspects of the incident, the arrested Prangon can be considered one of the key suspects in this case,” he told The Daily Star.

Prangon is a resident of Kachari Mor in the Bagichapara area of Durgapur municipality, police said.

Khandakar Shaker Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Durgapur Police Station, told The Daily Star that Prangon is the nephew of a local criminal known as “Shooter Shamim”, who faces at least 30 cases filed with the police station, including at least three murder cases.

The OC said Prangon was in police custody following the SRB operation and that legal procedures were under way to produce him before a court.

According to SRB sources, a team from the headquarters company of SRB-14 conducted the drive at the request of the investigating officer in the journalist Alif murder case. Using information technology and intelligence tracking, the team arrested Ashikur in the Shaheed Minar area before handing him over to the police station concerned.

Alif was the Netrokona correspondent for private IPTV channel Ruposhi Bangla. He also ran a Facebook page called “Detective Article”, where he published investigative reports on border smuggling and various other criminal activities and irregularities.

On the night of October 15, Alif was shot dead by criminals in the Telanjia area near Utrail Bazar on the Shyamganj-Birishiri road in Durgapur upazila.

The following day, his wife, Anandita Sangma, filed a murder case with Durgapur Police Station against seven to eight unidentified individuals.

Police arrested another suspect, 22-year-old Apurbo, on October 18 and sent him to jail by court order. He is currently on police remand.

The fishermen also hurled brickbats at a speedboat carrying Shariatpur-1 MP Sayed Ahmed Aslam, who escaped unhurt.

The incident occurred around 9:00am at Char Kolikal, a remote area of the Padma river in Palerchar union. During the drive, conducted from 4:00am to 12:30pm, the authorities detained 41 fishermen and seized a boat, three lakh metres of current nets and 30kg of mother hilsa, Shariatpur District Fisheries Officer Shwajit Kumar Deb told The Daily Star.

He said members of the Coast Guard, police, upazila administration and fisheries department launched the drive in the Zajira stretch of the Padma around 4:00am, with the local MP accompanying them. Before the operation, the MP had visited several riverside areas and held street meetings to raise awareness about protecting mother hilsa.

According to the fisheries officer, the team found fishermen gathered at Char Kolikal with boats, nets and other fishing equipment. When the drive began, the fishermen fled.

As the team attempted to seize nets, boats and other equipment left along the riverbank, a group of fishermen returned carrying brickbats, sticks and machetes and launched an attack.

The fishermen struck the team’s boats with sticks and brickbats, injuring two people participating in the operation. The team was forced to retreat in the face of the attack.

Additional river police and two army teams later arrived at the scene and joined the operation. The attackers fled when the joint forces launched a fresh drive, the district fisheries officer said.

Asked why he joined the operation, MP Sayed Ahmed Aslam said he had received allegations that a syndicate was helping fishermen circumvent the ban on catching mother hilsa by influencing the administration and other authorities.

“Most of those fishing are not genuine fishermen but outsiders. I joined the drive myself to verify the allegations,” he said.

The MP said he had joined the operation around 3:00am and that 41 people had been detained during raids in different areas. Although the detainees claimed to be fishermen, he said, the authorities had found no evidence to establish their identities as such.

A large number of those detained had come from other districts, he alleged, adding that a local syndicate had hired them to fish in the area.

He said specific allegations had been raised against the Majhirghat and Sureshwar river police outposts, with complainants claiming that the people involved had been allowed to fish after managing the relevant authorities.

The MP said he had asked the authorities concerned to investigate the allegations and take departmental action against those found responsible.

He added that his purpose was not merely to detain fishermen but also to counsel them and explain why they should not destroy the country’s natural resources.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Saeed Ibn Reza of the River Police’s Chandpur region told The Daily Star that 27 cases had been filed in the area over illegal hilsa fishing in the past 12 days.

He suggested that the allegations might have been made by the detainees, their relatives and family members because cases had been filed against those detained.

“I do not think there is any truth to these allegations. I am not aware of them,” he said.

However, he said the river police would take departmental action if an investigation established the allegations to be true.

Following today’s attack, the MP said the authorities would intensify their operations.

Photo: Collected The body of a local Jubo Dal leader was found at a bus counter in Magura town early today, with a puncture wound to the head.

The deceased was identified as Md Saker Hossain, 40. He was senior joint convener of the Magura municipality unit of Jubo Dal, said District Jubo Dal Convener Mizanur Rahman.

Magura Superintendent of Police Molla Azad Hossain said police had found a puncture wound on the back of the victim's head.

“We cannot confirm at this stage whether the injury was caused by a gunshot. The exact cause of death will be determined after receiving the autopsy report,” he said.

He added that necessary legal action would be taken based on the findings.

Hailed from Beparipara in the town’s Parnanduali area, he worked as a counter master at the bus terminal.

Family members alleged that Saker was killed in a premeditated attack motivated by political rivalry. They also said that he had faced 10 "politically motivated" cases over the past 17 years.

"My brother was shot dead in a premeditated plan due to political rivalry; we want justice," said the victim's brother Raj Mir.

According to local sources, residents found Saker unconscious inside the Royal Express counter at Magura Bus Terminal around 6:00am and rushed him to Magura 250-bed Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

Hospital authorities informed police after noticing a suspicious wound on the back of his head.

Dr Mainul Hasan of the hospital’s emergency department said Saker had died before being brought to the hospital.

“We found a puncture wound on the back of his head and informed police,” he said, adding that the body had been kept at the hospital morgue.

The victim, Ripon Mia, 45, was a vice-president of the Jubo Dal’s ward-7 unit in Bholabo union, said Mahfuzur Rahman Humayun, president of Rupganj upazila BNP.

The incident took place around 11:00pm in the Paiska area.

Ripon’s daughter Shila said, “Several men chased my father and hacked him. My father had a rivalry with them.”

Family members also alleged that Ripon had received death threats from his rivals.

According to local BNP activists, there had been a rivalry between supporters of Narayanganj-1 MP Mustafizur Rahman Bhuiyan and Kazi Moniruzzaman, former president of Narayanganj district BNP.Ripon was the supporter of MP Mustafizur.

The dispute intensified recently over whether certain names should be included in the guest list for a religious gathering, they said. Tensions flared between the two groups on Sunday night.

Ripon was chased by his rivals and critically injured with sharp weapons, said AHM Salauddin, officer-in-charge of Rupganj Police Station.

Family members took him to a local hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

When contacted for comment, neither MP Mustafizur nor Moniruzzaman responded to our phone calls.

BNP leader Mahfuzur told The Daily Star that the killing stemmed from a dispute over political dominance.

“There had been tensions between the two groups before, and the conflict intensified recently over a waz mahfil,” he said.

Victim’s son Shawon filed a murder case with Rupganj Police Station yesterday evening, naming seven accused and 30-40 others who were not identified.

File photo Dhaka-6 lawmaker Ishraque Hossain resigned from the council of ministers yesterday after facing growing criticism over his role in an “anti-drug drive” in which he was seen brandishing a firearm.

Ishraque, who on Sunday denied reports that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had earlier instructed him to resign, said he had voluntarily expressed his intention to quit as state minister for Liberation War Affairs.

“The official version would naturally be that I was asked to resign on the prime minister’s instructions, rather than at my own request,” he said at a media briefing at the Jatiya Press Club in the afternoon.

He said he wanted to resign to focus more on an anti-drug campaign and other public activities in Dhaka-6 and surrounding areas, and the prime minister had agreed to let him do that.

Defending his actions, Ishraque, son of former Dhaka City mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, said he would apologise if he had done anything wrong but maintained that he had committed no mistake during the drive.

Ishraque’s resignation letter was sent after the media briefing, said his press officer, Mahfuz Kabir Mukta.

The letter reached the cabinet division at 6:00pm yesterday, said one of its top officials, adding that it was forwarded to the Prime Minister’s Office.

A gazette notification related to the resignation could be issued at any time.

The controversy erupted after Ishraque posted a video on his Facebook account on Saturday of himself getting out of a vehicle with a pistol during an anti-drug drive in the capital’s Gendaria area.

Other footage appeared to show people accompanying him carrying firearms. In one video, a person was seen threatening to shoot, while another showed a bodyguard kicking a young man.

The following day, several media outlets reported that the prime minister had instructed him in the afternoon to step down.

Ishraque dubbed the news as false and fabricated, but at around 8:30am yesterday, he called the press conference.

There, he said confusion had arisen over the timing and process of the announcement: an official decision was supposed to be communicated through the prescribed process, but one of his colleagues disclosed the matter ahead of schedule.

Until the prime minister’s instructions were formally announced, the matter should be treated as a rumour or untrue, he said, adding that he received the formal decision on yesterday morning.

“Whether it happened yesterday or today, what difference does it make? It happened.”

Ishraque defended Saturday’s anti-drug operation, saying it had been coordinated with local law enforcement agencies and aimed at dismantling drug distribution networks.

He expressed disappointment that public discussion had focused on the firearm rather than the campaign.

Ghuntighar and Munshitek had become hubs for drug distribution, and the operation targeted drug dens, he said, adding that six people were handed over to police with evidence.

The local officers-in-charge and Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) deputy commissioners overseeing his constituency were aware of and involved in the operation, he said, describing it as part of efforts coordinated through the Dhaka-6 law and order committee.

The DMP, however, ordered an investigation into the incident, assigning the Wari division to look into it.

Ishraque said he had two firearms registered in his name and that one had been carried briefly for his protection.

The Firearms Policy 2025 allows licensed firearms for self-defence but bars their display in ways that may cause fear or annoyance.

He maintained that he had acted properly and wanted to ensure that no one was harmed.

“I believe I did the right thing in the proper way. I went there, risking my life. People may say that, though I do not care. If someone fires from a rooftop, we do not know whose head the bullet will hit.”

Locals had applauded the drive, he said, adding that he would continue working to meet their expectations.

He went on to urge the media and the public to focus on identifying the main suppliers behind drug distribution rather than concentrating only on street-level dealers.

Asked whether he was considering contesting the Dhaka mayoral election, the 39-year-old said the decision rested entirely with his party and its chairman.

He contested the 2020 mayoral election and had since worked on the capital’s problems under the party’s guidance.

“I am 100 percent prepared if the party decides to nominate me for the election,” he said, adding that he would make every effort to ensure the victory of whoever the party nominated.

Photo: Collected Around 50 vehicles were robbed in two separate incidents on the Eidgaon-Eidghar-Baishari road in Cox’s Bazar yesterday, passengers said.

The incidents took place at Himchhari Dhala in the afternoon, when a group of armed robbers intercepted CNG-run autorick-shaws and motorcycles, looting cash, mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint.

Victims said 10 to 12 masked men armed with weapons blocked vehicles and held passengers hostage. The robbers took some victims to a nearby forest, beat them up and robbed of their belongings.

Mohammad Robiul Islam, manager of a private organisation’s Eidghar branch, said he was travelling by motorcycle from Eidgaon Bazar to Eidghar with a colleague when the robbers stopped them at Himchhari Dhala and took Tk 1.2 lakh.

Abdul Hakim, an accountant at the Eidghar branch of another non-governmental organisation, said he was travelling to Eidghar Bazar from Eidgaon Bazar in an autorickshaw with two others when the robbers intercepted them.

The robbers held them at gunpoint and took Tk 1.5 lakh before taking them to a nearby forest and beating them, he said.

Jasim Uddin, acting chairman of Eidghar Union, said many vehicles had been robbed in two separate incidents. Police reached the scene after receiving information and launched an operation, he added.

Eidgaon Police Station Officer-in-Charge ATM Shifatul Majdar confirmed the incidents, saying the robbers had blocked the road, looted passengers and fled into the forest.

Several police teams were conducting operations to arrest those involved, but no one had been detained as of last night, he said.

While the officer could not confirm the number of vehicles robbed, several victims estimated that around 50 vehicles had been targeted.

Police and local sources said patrols had been stepped up along the road, while several teams were searching the surrounding hilly areas.

Local residents said robberies, abductions and looting frequently occur on the 17-kilometre road through the hilly areas of Ramu and Eidgaon upazilas. They said vehicular movement on the road usually stops after dusk because of security concerns.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order after the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) produced him before the court seeking a three-day remand, said Additional Public Prosecutor Muhammad Shamsud Doha Sumon.

According to a forwarding report submitted by police, investigators found that Agarwala allegedly laundered money and conducted illegal gold and diamond transactions for years under the cover of local and international jewellery businesses.

CID said its investigation found that Agarwala's company imported gold bars, jewellery, loose diamonds and other items worth Tk 38.47 crore through letters of credit between September 6, 2006, and February 8, 2024.

The agency also alleged that the company collected gold and diamonds worth Tk 678.19 crore from the local market through purchase, exchange and replacement methods.

“However, the company failed to show the CID valid documents regarding its sources or suppliers,” the report said.

CID filed the money laundering case with Gulshan Police Station on November 17 last year.

On Monday, members of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch arrested Dilip Agarwala from the capital's Banani area at CID's request in connection with the case.

Earlier, on September 3, 2024, he was arrested by the then Rapid Action Battalion in a case over the killing of teenager Hridoy Ahmed during July Uprising. He was subsequently released on bail.

Agarwala is a former president of the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS), a former vice-president and director of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI), and a member of the Awami League's central industry and commerce subcommittee.

The death toll was more than two-and-a-half times the 73 deaths recorded in political clashes during the same period.

The incidents of mob violence reportedly stemmed from allegations of theft, robbery, mugging, rape and hurting religious sentiments, as well as attempts to establish dominance.

The report, signed by HRSS Executive Director Ijajul Islam, was compiled using reports from 16 national dailies and the organisation’s investigations between January and September.

According to the report, 1,013 incidents of political violence left 73 dead and 6,473 injured. Of these, 931 incidents, or 91 percent, involved BNP infighting or clashes with rival parties.

BNP infighting alone accounted for 342 incidents, leaving 40 dead and 2,632 injured. Among the 73 people killed in political violence, 46 were from the BNP, eight from Jamaat-e-Islami and six from the Awami League.

More than 270 political cases named 5,809 individuals and accused 32,433 unnamed people. Of the 5,644 people arrested, 4,827 belonged to the AL.

At least 17 people died in law enforcement custody or in incidents involving torture, shootings and so-called “gunfights”, while 10 died while fleeing police chases.

Another 95 inmates, including 55 undertrial prisoners, 20 AL men and one BNP activist, died in jail.

Under the Cyber Protection Ordinance 2025 and Cyber Protection Act 2026, 113 people were sued and 55 arrested in 40 cases. Another 12 were detained over objectionable posts about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and 24 for allegedly hurting religious sentiments.

Fifty-one journalists were sued in 19 cyber cases. Overall, 518 journalists faced attacks or harassment in 288 incidents, leaving 297 injured and 20 arrested.

Police also foiled 58 rallies, leaving 439 people injured and 46 detained.

Along the Indian border, 43 attacks by the BSF killed 13 Bangladeshis and injured 39. Landmines laid by the Arakan Army along the Myanmar border killed eight and injured five.

The report also recorded abuse of 2,404 women and girls. At least 657 were raped, including 392 minors and 130 gang-rape victims, while 29 were murdered after rape.

Domestic violence claimed the lives of 457 women, while 494 children died in 1,810 incidents of abuse.

Meanwhile, 56 attacks on minorities resulted in the vandalism of 21 temples and 47 homes, while 535 workers died in workplace incidents.

Photo: Collected Around 50 vehicles were reportedly robbed in two incidents on the Eidgaon-Eidghar-Baishari road in Cox’s Bazar on Monday, according to victims.

The incidents took place at Himchhari Dhala in the afternoon, when 10-12 masked men armed with weapons intercepted CNG-run autorickshaws and motorcycles and looted cash, mobile phones and other valuables at gunpoint.

Victims said the robbers took some passengers to a nearby forest, beat them and robbed them of their belongings.

Mohammad Robiul Islam, manager of a private organisation’s Eidghar branch, said the robbers stopped his motorcycle while he was travelling from Eidgaon Bazar to Eidghar with a colleague and took Tk 1.2 lakh.

Abdul Hakim, an accountant at another NGO’s Eidghar branch, said the robbers intercepted the autorickshaw he was on with two others, took Tk 1.5 lakh, and beat them in a nearby forest.

Jasim Uddin, acting chairman of Eidghar Union, said police arrived after receiving information and launched an operation.

Eidgaon Police Station Officer-in-Charge ATM Shifatul Majdar confirmed the incidents, saying the robbers fled into the forest. Several police teams were searching for them, but no one had been detained as of Monday night.

The officer could not confirm the number of vehicles targeted, but victims estimated it at around 50.

Police and local sources said patrols had been stepped up and teams were searching the surrounding hills.

Locals said robberies, abductions and looting frequently occur along the 17-kilometre road through Ramu and Eidgaon upazilas. Locals usually stop using the road after dusk because of security concerns.

Photo: Courtesy The family of Nazrul Islam, one of the two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia on October 14, yesterday alleged that Saudi authorities had executed him without notifying them beforehand or giving him an opportunity to defend himself.

Nazrul, 22, the eldest of four siblings, left for Saudi Arabia on November 10, 2022, and worked as a cleaner, according to his family.

Six months after his departure, Saudi police arrested him and a Bangladeshi woman for allegedly committing an “immoral act” at a mosque in Makkah.

More than three years later, his family said it learnt from media reports that he had been executed in Makkah on October 14.

His mother said he spoke to the family by phone from prison every Sunday, but they received no advance notice of his execution.

However, it could not yet be independently verified what charges Nazrul faced, whether he received legal assistance, or whether he was given an opportunity to defend himself before his execution.

The Bangladesh government has yet to officially verify the identities of the two people executed.

Nazrul’s father Abdul Basir said, “If my son was executed without just cause, I want justice.”

Rahima Begum, Nazrul’s mother, has repeatedly broken down in tears since learning of her son’s death. The family also said Nazrul’s paternal aunt, Abeda Begum, died of a heart attack after hearing the news on Wednesday night.

The family has urged the government to investigate the circumstances surrounding his execution and arrange for his body to be brought home at state expense. Neighbours have also called for support for the family.

Nazrul’s father, who had borrowed Tk 7 lakh to send his son to Saudi Arabia, also spoke of how the creditors were now pressuring him to repay the debt.

Contacted, Brahmanbaria Deputy Commissioner Md Abu Sayeed said, “We have received no instructions from higher authorities, and the family has not submitted any application either. If the body is brought back to Bangladesh, we will provide assistance in accordance with the rules, as he was a resident of Brahmanbaria.”

Meanwhile, the Bangladesh government has yet to officially confirm that the two people executed in Saudi Arabia were Bangladeshi nationals and has sought an explanation from Riyadh over an apparent lapse in information-sharing.

Speaking to reporters at the foreign ministry yesterday afternoon, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said media reports had identified the two as Bangladeshis, but the government was still seeking further details.

An official at the Bangladesh mission in Jeddah, speaking on condition of anonymity, told The Daily Star that both were executed on charges of “adultery”.

The official said Saudi authorities had provided only names and offences, making it difficult to verify their identities or establish whether they were the two who had been executed.

Stressing that the two countries maintain strong bilateral ties and are both signatories to the Vienna Convention,, Humaiun said,”So why was there a gap in the exchange of information? We have sought an explanation from Saudi Arabia.

“There is definitely a gap here, a lapse somewhere in the process, and we are trying to determine the extent of the issue. At the same time, it is deeply disappointing that the executions took place over these alleged offences.”

The state minister also said Bangladesh expected Saudi Arabia to share information about detained Bangladeshi nationals, just as Dhaka would if Saudi nationals were detained in Bangladesh.

“If we detain any Saudi national here, we will certainly inform Saudi Arabia so that consular services can be extended to that person. Similarly, we expect the same for Bangladeshis.”

According to the foreign ministry, the two were accused of committing “adultery” inside a mosque in Makkah.

Saudi authorities arrested, tried and executed them without notifying Dhaka in advance. Bangladesh learnt of the executions on October 14 and subsequently sought details from Riyadh.

Opposition Leader and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman yesterday questioned the roles of the government and the Bangladesh mission in Saudi Arabia following the execution of two Bangladeshis.

In a Facebook post around 7:30pm, Shafiqur said, “The government and the Bangladesh embassy are bound to make their positions clear on this matter.”

He pointed out that a large number of Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia and other Middle Eastern countries, and that Bangladesh maintains diplomatic missions abroad to safeguard the interests of expatriates, as well as the country’s dignity and national interests.

The tribunal set October 15 for the prosecution’s opening statement and recording of the first witness’s testimony.

Mesbah described how law enforcement personnel shot private university students in Badda and Rampura on July 18 and 19.

Seven-month-old Rakib was taken from a paediatric ward on September 19, while a six-day-old newborn was stolen from the Special Care Newborn Unit, a restricted ward, on October 9. No arrests have been made.

In the first incident, an unidentified woman allegedly took Rakib, leaving behind a three-month-old baby, later sent to a child care facility in Chattogram.

Rakib’s father, Mohammad Rubel Hossain, said his son was admitted with pneumonia on September 15. On September 19, a woman offered to calm the crying child and took him in her arms. Later, she disappeared with the baby.

CCTV footage reportedly showed the woman leaving in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw with two other girls. The family searched in Ukhiya after learning the vehicle had headed towards Sonarpara, but found no trace of Rakib. A general diary was filed on September 20.

In the second incident, a woman allegedly took a newborn from SCANU around 11:25pm on October 9.

Hospital records show the suspect was seen near the breastfeeding room before entering the ward and leaving through the emergency department with the baby.

The child’s mother, Rozina Akter, said she had fed and cleaned her son before returning to her room. She began searching around 2:30am after someone enquired about the baby.

“I just want my child back in a healthy condition,” she said.

Sub-Inspector Rajib Pal, investigating the second case, said the suspect could not be clearly identified from CCTV footage as she wore a mask and burqa. Most hospital cameras were not working, he added.

Police said both cases were under investigation, with no conclusive evidence linking them.

Hospital Superintendent Dr Mong Ting Nyo said repeated requests for police personnel had not secured the required deployment.

Additional Superintendent of Police Ahidur Rahman said four to five officers were stationed at the hospital’s police box. He called for reviewing internal security and considering redeployment of Ansar members.

Resident Medical Officer Dr Shantanu Ghosh said a three-member investigation committee had sought more time to collect statements and examine CCTV footage, as several external cameras were faulty or produced unclear images.

Police recovered three motorcycles based on their statements.

Khulshi Police Station Sub-Inspector Md Nasim told The Daily Star confirmed the incident.

The arrestees are police constable Anik Das, 27; Wahid Md Jebel Hossain alias Anik Wahid, 39; Mohiuddin Selim, 52; and Wahed Nasir alias Diamond, 38.

Among them, Anik Das is a constable who was attached to Rajarbagh Police Lines under the sports quota from Bandarban Police Lines, the OC said.

Earlier, Mohammad Apu, 22, a resident of Companiganj upazila in Noakhali, had filed a general diary (GD) after being robbed. After the constable was detained, police registered the GD as a case.

According to the case statement, Apu and his friends were travelling from Noakhali to Cox’s Bazar on three motorcycles on the night of October 16. Around 1:30am on October 17, when they reached Zakir Hossain Road in front of Foy’s Lake Eye Hospital under Khulshi Police Station, a maroon-and-black private car and two motorcycles blocked their way.

Several people allegedly held them hostage and took their motorcycle keys. Apu was beaten and injured before the assailants threatened him with sharp weapons, forced him into the private car and rode away with his motorcycle.

After driving him around different roads in the city, they took him to the Shershah area under Bayezid Bostami Police Station around 3:00am. They took his Tecno mobile phone, worth about Tk 20,000, and left him by the roadside.

The stolen motorcycle was an on-test Yamaha sports bike valued at around Tk 5.5 lakh, according to the case statement.

“Anik Das asked Apu to come to the police box in front of the Bayezid Link Road, where Apu informed the Khulshi police. Anik Das was subsequently arrested there with the assistance of Khulshi police,” Nasim said.

Based on information provided by Anik, police arrested Wahid and Mohiuddin Selim in the BITAK Bazar area under Pahartali Police Station. During interrogation, they said the motorcycle was in the custody of Wahed Nasir alias Diamond.

Police recovered the motorcycle from a garage in the Faiyaltali Bazar area under Pahartali Police Station around 4:30am on October 20. Three motorcycles, including the stolen one, were recovered from the suspects’ possession.

Jinia Chakma, additional superintendent of police (crime and operations) of Bandarban Police, told The Daily Star, “We were informed about the incident, and departmental action has already been taken against him.”

Police are trying to arrest other alleged gang members and recover the private car used in the robbery.

Photo: Collected A court in Netrokona has placed Opurba, 22, on a four-day remand in connection with the murder of journalist Lutfozzaman Fakir Alif in Durgapur.

The order was passed this afternoon after police produced him before the Durgapur Chowki Court at the end of a previous one-day remand and sought a fresh seven-day remand.

Khandakar Shaker Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Durgapur Police Station, confirmed the development. He said Nurul Amin Bhuiyan, judge of the Senior Judicial Magistrate's Court, granted a four-day remand after the hearing.

Earlier on Sunday, the court had placed Opurba on a one-day remand following a police petition. He remained in police custody yesterday.

“Considerable information has been obtained during questioning. These details are being verified. However, for a thorough investigation of the incident, he needs to be interrogated further,” OC Khandakar Shaker Ahmed told The Daily Star.

Investigation sources said Opurba was arrested after midnight on Saturday in front of the old cinema hall in Durgapur municipal town.

Police claimed Opurba was present at the crime scene during Alif's murder, carrying a bag containing weapons. They also said he admitted this during preliminary interrogation.

The OC said Opurba is the nephew of the prime suspect and alleged shooter in the killing. The suspect is known to be a professional killer, and investigators obtained information indicating that the firearms used in the murder had been kept in Opurba's custody.

According to case documents, Alif was shot dead by criminals around 8:00pm on October 15 while returning home after having tea at a stall in the Telanjia area of Durgapur upazila.

The following day, his wife, Anandita Sangma, filed a murder case with Durgapur Police Station, accusing seven to eight unidentified individuals.

DB’s Uttara division conducted the raid and seized alcohol, yaba and cannabis from the plot belonging to Additional Deputy Inspector General of Police Abdullah Al Jahir, an officer from the 24th police batch.

Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (detective) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told The Daily Star that Jahir had rented out the plot, where drug use and illegal “DJ parties” had allegedly been going on for a long time, prompting police to conduct the raid.

Elias Kabir, deputy commissioner of DB’s Uttara division, said parties and drug consumption were regularly reported at the property in Police Housing-1. He alleged that Jahir was the primary organiser of the parties.

Elias said a man named Mahbub Alam acted as the co-organiser. According to DB, Mahbub told investigators that Jahir received 70 percent of the earnings from the parties, while he took the rest.

The property was available for bookings through the US-based platform Airbnb, and "DJ parties" were regularly organised for those who booked it, DB sources said.

Elias said the arrestees had been sent for summary trial.

Meanwhile, Jahir was attached to the Police Headquarters following the incident.

Speaking to The Daily Star, Jahir said that his plot had facilities for hosting birthday parties and family gatherings. They take bookings through Airbnb, but drugs and "DJ parties" are prohibited under their rules. Those who violated the restrictions were blacklisted and fined, he said.

Regarding last night’s incident, Jahir said the property had been rented out for a birthday party, but the guests brought drugs, which were recovered during the DB raid.

“What is our crime here? We rented out the property. Our guidelines explicitly prohibit drugs and DJ parties. Those found with drugs committed criminal offences,” he said. He also claimed that two to three parties were held at the venue each month, dismissing allegations that such parties were organised there every day.

Nahid Islam is likely to remain convener, and Akhter Hossen the member secretary.

The positions of chief organiser, chief coordinator and spokesperson will be abolished, with Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah tipped to become senior joint conveners.

Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and Sarjis Alam are likely to become senior joint member secretaries.

The restructuring aims to strengthen its grassroots activities ahead of local government polls and its first national council next February, they added.

The revised central committee and political council lists were initially expected yesterday but are now likely to be announced today or tomorrow, after Nahid returns from visits to Shariatpur and Madaripur.

Two senior leaders, speaking anonymously, said Samantha and Niva were left out because they resigned from the party council before the national election in protest against the NCP joining the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance.

Both remain party members and members of its advisory committee but have largely been inactive in organisational activities.

Under the proposed structure, at least 10 of the 16 Political Council members will serve as joint conveners, overseeing specialised subcommittees and policy work. They include Abdullah Al Amin, Ariful Islam Adeeb, Atiq Mujahid, Abdul Hannan Masud, Ali Ahsan Junaid, Sarwar Tushar, Akram Hossain, Saleh Uddin Sifat, Mahmuda Alam Mitu and Nusrat Tabassum.

The party also plans to distribute around 30 specialised cell portfolios covering areas including international relations, administration, finance, human rights and law.

Another 10-11 joint conveners and seven to eight joint member secretaries are expected to be appointed to expand the central committee beyond the Political Council.

A 23-member Organisational Subcommittee, led by Sarjis Alam, has been formed to strengthen grassroots activities.

The party is also considering changes to the top leadership of its women’s wing, Jatiya Nari Shakti. Five leaders -- Mahmuda Alam Mitu, Monira Sharmeen, Nusrat Tabassum, Humaira Noor and Manjila Jhuma -- are being considered for the posts of convener, member secretary and organising secretary.

A senior party leader said Monira Sharmeen, Manjila Jhuma and Humaira Noor had been recommended for positions among the party’s top five leaders. The proposal remains under consideration.

Sarwar Tusher, an NCP Political Council member, told The Daily Star that the changes were being made ahead of local government elections expected within a year and the party’s first national council next year.

“The final list will be officially released very soon,” he said.

“Chaos and partisanship in the appointment of fertiliser dealers and in the fertiliser crisis are going beyond all limits,” Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar said while speaking at a press conference at the party's central office in Moghbazar, Dhaka this afternoon.

Many members of upazila and district fertiliser and seed monitoring committees, he alleged, had been nominated on political considerations.

“Political influence in dealer appointments has now become institutionalised,” he said.

He said clear policies govern fertiliser imports, distribution and dealer appointments, but these were being violated.

Under the policy, no family can hold more than one dealership. Applicants must be residents of the relevant union and have their own godowns and sufficient financial capacity.

“Everything has been violated, one after another,” he alleged.

Golam Porwar further claimed that ruling party MPs and leaders had divided among themselves the number of dealerships each would appoint and were awarding them in exchange for money.

He also questioned the government's own fertiliser figures. Citing Agriculture Minister Mohammed Aminur Rashid, he said the country's total fertiliser demand for the 2026-27 fiscal year stood at 58 lakh tonnes, while government estimates indicated stocks were about nine lakh tonnes higher than demand.

“If there is enough fertiliser against demand, why is there a shortage? Then this is a hundred per cent failure of the government in distribution,” he said.

At the press conference, Jamaat demanded an immediate investigation into the allegations and punishment for those found guilty.

The party also called for the publication of the criteria for dealer appointments, the process for preparing candidate lists and the basis for granting licences

Asked whether Jamaat itself wanted fertiliser dealerships, Golam Porwar said, “Our MPs do not distribute any fertiliser; they have no dealerships.”

“Our complaint is not why we didn't get any or why we weren't given any,” he added, saying qualified and genuine businesspeople should receive the dealerships.

Asked about the ongoing movement of the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance, he said Jamaat was playing a “non-violent, responsible and constructive” role.

But the 39-year-old Dhaka-6 MP had repeatedly embarrassed his party over the years, even as his popularity among its rank and file grew.

Ultimately, it was his pistol-wielding, drug-busting “operation” that cost him his post as state minister for Liberation War affairs.

Ishraque’s father, Sadeque Hossain Khoka, was an influential BNP leader with a strong following in the constituency. Ishraque became active in politics around the 2018 national election and soon established himself as a formidable organiser on the streets.

In 2020, he ran for mayor of Dhaka South but lost to the Awami League candidate before challenging the result. He was declared victorious in 2025 but was never sworn in. He then contested the 2026 parliamentary election and won the Dhaka-6 seat.

Here is a look back at some of his most talked-about moments.

The hero who snatched a BNP activist from police

On February 13, 2023, a rally was held in front of the National Press Club to protest a move to revoke the gallantry award conferred on BNP founder Ziaur Rahman.

During the rally, police were about to detain a BNP activist injured in a baton charge when Ishraque intervened, jostling with officers and pulling the activist away. He was also injured in the scuffle.

Ishraque later shared a video of the incident on Facebook, which went viral. He declared that neither baton charges nor cannon fire would stop him from protecting a party worker as long as he was alive.

The incident propelled him into the spotlight and earned him immense popularity among BNP activists.

A presser with Biden’s ‘adviser’

On October 28, 2023, following clashes surrounding BNP’s grand rally, a man named Zahidul Islam, alias Mia Arefi, appeared at the party’s Naya Paltan office, claiming to be an adviser to then US president Joe Biden.

He spoke to journalists while seated beside Ishraque and retired lieutenant general Chowdhury Hasan Sarwardy. The next day, police detained Arefi at the airport, and all three were named in a case filed with Paltan Police Station.

Ishraque and Sarwardy were accused of helping Arefi address journalists under a false identity.

The incident caused major embarrassment for the BNP, which issued a statement distancing itself from Arefi’s activities. Ishraque later expressed regret on Facebook.

After the July Uprising toppled the Awami League government and the courts ruled in favour of Ishraque’s claim to the mayoral post, his battle for office took a new turn.

In May 2025, he and his supporters laid siege to city hall after the interim government declined to administer his oath of office. Essential services were disrupted, causing public sufferings.

Ishraque even threatened to swear himself into office. While his loyalists saw the protests as a show of strength, the disruption and mounting public sufferings drew flak.

Eventually, Ishraque backed down without ever assuming office as mayor.

Ishraque went viral again on December 22, 2025, but this time for pushing and shoving his own party men to make his way to the front of a crowd.

He had visited the grave of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman to pay respects with the newly formed Bangladesh Jatiyotabadi Muktijoddha Projonmo.

He later expressed regret on Facebook but, as he would do repeatedly, offered an explanation that only deepened his embarrassment. He said he was being “firm” in “setting the lines right”.

Ishraque made headlines again during the swearing-in of newly elected members of parliament on February 17, 2026. Arriving late, he missed the oath-taking ceremony with his party colleagues and had to join the opposition and independent MPs instead.

Although Ishraque abstained from taking the oath as a member of the Constitution Reform Council, in line with his party’s decision, he appeared unsure what to do next.

Then he spotted independent MP Rumeen Farhana hurriedly gathering her belongings and leaving the hall after taking the parliamentary oath. Ishraque promptly followed her out, seemingly relieved to have found a cue.

Saluting with the service chiefs

Last July, after Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took over as president, he visited the National Memorial in Savar to pay tribute to the martyrs.

Ishraque, then state minister for Liberation War affairs, was among those present, alongside the chiefs of the three defence services.

When the three chiefs lined up and saluted the martyrs, Ishraque, standing alongside them, raised his hand in salute too. It was another viral moment, sparking a flood of memes.

Ishraque later said his hand rose in salute almost on its “own volition” whenever “freedom fighters” were mentioned, and that he would continue saluting them whenever and wherever he could.

Ishraque’s ministry organised a reception for martyrs’ families and July fighters at Agargaon to mark the second anniversary of the July Uprising.

Leaders of the National Citizen Party alleged that a documentary screened at the event failed to accurately portray the movement, leading to heated exchanges.

Instead of defusing the tension, Ishraque took the podium and began shouting, further angering the protesters. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed also failed to calm the situation, and the protesters eventually walked out of the venue.

On October 17, 2026, Ishraque jumped out of a car, pistol in hand.

He ran towards men attempting to flee, followed by his team of activists, who manhandled and kicked those they suspected of being drug peddlers. At least one of his associates was also seen brandishing a firearm.

Ishraque pointed his pistol at the suspects, while someone off-camera threatened to shoot.

The close-up video clips suggested that the MP even had his PR team on hand to film his exploits. That such vigilantism could go horribly wrong with the slightest misstep, and that it was entirely beyond his authority, appeared to have escaped the Dhaka-6 MP.

His subsequent statements suggested that he had confused lawmaking with policing. As for his explanation, Ishraque claimed he had drawn the pistol in “self-defence”.

They said constitutional reform should define the powers of state organs and ensure accountability.

The proposals came at a meeting between academics and the special parliamentary committee on constitutional reform at the Jatiya Sangsad yesterday.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, chair of the committee, said he was unsure whether the opposition’s absence would trigger controversy, but there would be opportunities for debate.

Responding to academic Ali Riaz’s concern that reform could become a partisan agenda without opposition participation, Salahuddin said the government was working to implement the July National Charter.

Opposition leaders would be welcome if they submitted their names, he said, adding that the initiative would proceed even without them.

At the meeting, academics said majoritarian politics and the “winner takes all” principle fuel discrimination and autocracy. Checks and balances and accountability were needed to prevent political parties from becoming ruling establishments after taking power.

Proposals included defining the judiciary’s authority over constitutional interpretation and fundamental principles, ensuring judicial accountability and establishing a separate constitutional court. One academic proposed a mechanism to hold courts accountable for violating the Constitution.

Discussions on the caretaker government system included removing the president’s role as a last-resort option and involving the judiciary if consensus could not be reached on earlier alternatives.

National Professor Mahbub Ullah said a constitutional amendment or a new constitution should reflect the views of political parties, intellectuals, professionals and ordinary citizens.

He proposed bringing state agencies that exercise coercive powers, including intelligence agencies, under accountability mechanisms.

Prof Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan said proposals had been made to recognise the Liberation War and those who contributed to the independence movement before and during the war.

Prof Samina Luthfa said proposals had been made to ensure women’s equal rights through legal amendments and replacing “Mohila” with “Nari” (woman), “Upajati” with “different ethnic communities” and “Upasampraday” with “religious communities” throughout the Constitution, as the existing terms carry discriminatory implications.

Forty-five academics were invited to the meeting, but only 17 attended.

Photo: Star State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain today said he had sought voluntary resignation from his post to focus on an anti-drug campaign in Dhaka-6 and surrounding areas, rejecting reports that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had instructed him to step down.

“I told the prime minister that I want to resign because I believe this anti-drug campaign has only just begun and must continue,” he said while speaking at a press conference at the Jatiya Press Club, adding that he did not want the controversy surrounding him to overshadow the government's work or embarrass his party.

The state minister came under criticism after videos circulated on social media showing him carrying a firearm during an "anti-drug" operation near the Ghuntighar railway crossing in Dhaka's Gandaria area on Saturday.

Defending the operation, Ishraque said the area, including Ghuntighar and Munshitek, had become a hub for drug distribution. He said the drive targeted several makeshift drug dens and that six people were detained and handed over to police along with the evidence seized.

He claimed the operation was conducted in coordination with local law enforcement agencies under decisions taken by the law and order committee for the Dhaka-6 constituency. Local police officials, including the officer-in-charge and the deputy commissioners concerned, were aware of the operation, he said.

“I did not go there to grab land or collect extortion money. I went there to fight for humanity,” he said, rejecting what he described as attempts to divert attention from the anti-drug campaign.

Explaining why he was seen carrying a firearm, Ishraque said he had briefly held his licenced weapon for his own protection. He maintained that he had done nothing wrong and apologised to anyone who might have been hurt by the operation.

He criticised media coverage of the incident, saying the focus had shifted from the campaign against drugs to the firearm and his actions. He argued that identifying major suppliers, rather than targeting only street-level distributors, was essential to tackling the drug trade.

“We will not be able to bring the situation under control until we identify and apprehend the main suppliers,” he said, urging journalists and members of the public to provide information about drug hotspots and those behind the trade.

Ishraque said the campaign would continue in Dhaka-6 and neighbouring areas, with a focus on identifying those behind drug distribution. He added that the prime minister had agreed to his request to concentrate on constituency-level work and other public concerns.

Responding to questions, Ishraque said two firearms were registered in his name. Citing security concerns, he said he had temporarily handed over his second firearm to another person who also held a licence.

He said police were sometimes reluctant to enter areas where drug dealers allegedly fired from rooftops, adding that he had faced strong pressure from people in his constituency to take action against drug-related activities.

“I believe I did the right thing in the proper way. I made sure that not a single person was harmed in the process,” he said.

Ishraque said he had explained his position to the prime minister and sought permission to step down from his ministerial responsibilities so that he could concentrate on work at the constituency level.

He said the prime minister had agreed to let him continue the anti-drug campaign.

“The official version would naturally be that I was asked to resign on the prime minister’s instructions, rather than at my own request,” he added.

Ishraque said the operation was necessary and that he had acted in response to public demand. He said residents had welcomed the drive, reiterating that his focus would remain on meeting their expectations and taking action against those involved in criminal activities.
