“They did not even wait six minutes after taking the oath before deceiving the people,” he said at a discussion titled “Proposed Amendments to the Cyber Security Act: The Future of Freedom of Expression and Civil Rights” at the Jatiya Press Club this noon.

The NCP’s Reform Implementation Committee organised the event.

Akhter said BNP lawmakers had not taken the oath as members of the Constitutional Reform Council. Instead, he alleged, they had moved to amend the constitution according to their preferences, using their two-thirds majority in parliament.

He said the constitutional amendment committee formed by the government reflected neither the referendum verdict nor the views of the people.

“Through a one-party committee formed to amend the constitution, the government is moving towards amending the constitution in the footsteps of the Awami League,” he said.

Akhter warned that using a two-thirds majority to keep state power under the party’s control would not bode well for the BNP.

The BNP, however, has said the constitutional amendment process will not be unilateral. Ruling party members of the committee have said commitments in the July National Charter, as well as those in the BNP’s election manifesto, will be taken into consideration.

Criticising the government’s proposed amendments to the Cyber Security Act, Akhter said the definition of offences was being broadened to such an extent that even criticism of the government could be labelled as rumours, defamation or misinformation, potentially allowing opposition leaders, activists and ordinary people to be arrested.

He said journalists and ordinary people had faced harassment through the misuse of the Digital Security Act during the Awami League’s rule.

Akhter also criticised the BNP government over the law and order situation, alleging that it was failing to take effective action despite incidents of extortion and looting across the country.

He said the home minister was busy with constitutional amendments instead of focusing on his ministry’s responsibilities. If the minister wanted to work on the constitution, Akhter said, he could be appointed an adviser on constitutional affairs rather than remain in charge of the home ministry.

Referring to the suspension of a Directorate of Youth Development recruitment examination over allegations of a question paper leak, Akhter demanded compensation for affected jobseekers. He also called for those involved in the leak to be identified and brought to justice.

Educationist Dr Nabila Idris presented the keynote paper at the event.

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() { // Share dropdown toggle const shareToggle = document.querySelector('.share-toggle'); const shareMenu = document.querySelector('.share-menu'); if (shareToggle && shareMenu) { shareToggle.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); shareMenu.classList.toggle('hidden'); }); // Close dropdown when clicking outside document.addEventListener('click', function() { shareMenu.classList.add('hidden'); }); shareMenu.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); } // Copy link functionality const copyBtn = document.querySelector('.copy-link-btn'); if (copyBtn) { copyBtn.addEventListener('click', function() { const url = this.getAttribute('data-url'); navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function() { // Show success message const originalText = copyBtn.innerHTML; copyBtn.innerHTML = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(function() { copyBtn.innerHTML = originalText; }, 2000); }); }); } }); Mohiuddin Alamgir Mohiuddin Alamgir The special parliamentary committee on constitutional reform will prioritise implementing the BNP’s agenda in line with its election manifesto alongside the July charter, ruling party members of the committee have said.

Key BNP proposals include restoring “Absolute trust and faith in Almighty Allah” as a fundamental state principle, excluding the judiciary and the president from the caretaker government system, and limiting an individual’s tenure as prime minister to 10 years.

The BNP also favours allowing the prime minister to simultaneously serve as the party chief and introducing the post of vice-president.

Committee members Chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni and Zainul Abdin confirmed the party’s position on the matter to The Daily Star, saying that constitutional matters included in the manifesto would be considered alongside the charter.

Committee Chair and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed reiterated that the BNP would fully implement the charter exactly as it was signed.

“Under our election manifesto, we have several proposals that require constitutional amendments, and we will include them too since we secured the people’s mandate on those issues,” he said at a recent media briefing.

The BNP manifesto says the July National Charter, signed on October 17, 2025, will be implemented with the highest priority.

It also promises to restore “Absolute trust and faith in Almighty Allah” to the constitution.

Former attorney general Mahmudul Islam writes in his book “Constitutional Law of Bangladesh” that in 1977, then president Ziaur Rahman issued a proclamation order adding the expression “Bismillah-Ar-Rahman-Ar-Rahim” before the preamble of the constitution.

“Under our election manifesto, we have several proposals that require constitutional amendments, and we will include them too since we secured the people’s mandate on those issues.” Salahuddin Ahmed, committee chair and home minister The words “nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism” were replaced with “Absolute trust and faith in the Almighty Allah, nationalism, democracy and socialism meaning economic and social justice”, Mahmudul wrote.

The change was incorporated into the constitution through the fifth amendment in 1979.

The 15th amendment, passed during the Awami League regime in 2011, removed “Absolute trust and faith in Almighty Allah” and restored that part of the constitution to the original 1972 wording.

Salahuddin pointed out that the principle of faith in the Almighty was also enshrined in article 8 as a fundamental principle and said even the opposition agreed on the matter.

In line with the July charter and its manifesto, the BNP pledged an “election-time, neutral caretaker government” to ensure free and fair national polls and give the system a permanent constitutional and institutional form.

While the caretaker framework is to be settled through discussions based on the July charter, BNP is opposed to involving the judiciary and the president in the system.

The July charter sets out a series of steps for appointing the head of the caretaker government. The process begins with the formation of a five-member panel comprising the prime minister, opposition leader, speaker, deputy speaker from the opposition and a representative of the second-largest opposition party. The panel will select a caretaker chief from a list of nominees submitted by political parties and independents.

If the panel fails to reach a decision, the charter provides for a second step. At one stage, it proposes bringing in an Appellate Division judge and a High Court judge, turning the panel into a seven-member body to vote on a shortlist.

Several parties, including the BNP, objected to this provision.

The BNP also pledged that a person could serve as prime minister for a maximum of 10 years, whether consecutive or non-consecutive.

The July charter, however, says the prime minister cannot simultaneously serve as the party chief, a provision opposed by BNP and its allies.

The party further pledged to ensure a balance of power between the president and prime minister and to strengthen judicial independence.

It proposed introducing a 100-member upper chamber of parliament, with seats distributed in proportion to the number of seats parties secure in the lower house.

Most other parties, however, agreed that the upper chamber should be constituted in proportion to the percentage of votes secured by parties in the national election.

BNP also promised to amend article 70 to allow MPs to vote against their party line except in cases involving no-confidence motions, money bills, constitutional amendments and national security, including wartime situations.

The July charter does not list constitutional amendments or national security as exceptions.

The BNP pledged to enact necessary laws for the formation of the Public Service Commission and Anti-Corruption Commission and for appointments to the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General. It also proposed transforming the Public Service Commission into a stronger institution for recruitment in education, health and other sectors.

The governor of Bangladesh Bank and the chairperson and members of the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission would be appointed by the government in accordance with law.

A majority of parties in the July charter agreed that the president should appoint the chiefs of the National Human Rights Commission, Information Commission, Bangladesh Press Council, Law Commission and Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission, as well as the governor of Bangladesh Bank.

The BNP pledged that the president would appoint the chief justice from among the two most senior judges of the Appellate Division, in accordance with the constitutional provision.

A majority of the parties in the July charter, however, agreed that the president should appoint the senior-most Appellate Division judge as chief justice.

The BNP also proposed appointing an Ombudsman. The “Tax Ombudsman”, introduced during a previous BNP tenure, was widely considered effective. The July charter proposes that a search committee headed by the speaker recommend names to the president for appointment as the Ombudsman.

BNP’s manifesto promises that one of the deputy speakers in each chamber of parliament would be nominated from the opposition.

It also pledged that opposition MPs would chair the Public Accounts Committee, Privileges Committee, Estimates Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings of the National Parliament. Chairpersons of other standing committees would also be appointed from the opposition in proportion to the number of seats they hold in parliament.

The BNP pledged that the Supreme Court would have a permanent seat in the capital, while the chief justice could establish permanent benches in each division. It also proposed further strengthening the Supreme Judicial Council and expanding its jurisdiction.

Necessary constitutional amendments would be made to place control over the service terms and conditions of subordinate court judges entirely with the Supreme Court.

A permanent prosecution/attorney service would gradually be established at the district level through law.

On the president’s power of pardon, the BNP proposed adding a constitutional provision stating that the president may grant pardon, reprieve and respite for any sentence and remit, suspend or reduce any sentence, but must exercise that power in accordance with standards, principles and procedures prescribed by law.

Local government elections would be held under the direct supervision of the Election Commission, with necessary laws enacted for the purpose.

Appropriate laws would govern the financial management of local government institutions to ensure their effective autonomy, while the relationship between local government bodies and government officers and employees working with them would also be determined by law.

The BNP proposed forming a police commission to ensure professionalism and accountability and make police services more people-friendly. The relevant ordinance would be reviewed, reformed and enacted as appropriate law.

It also proposed reviewing in parliament the formation of an independent criminal investigation service.

Existing laws would be properly applied in investigating and prosecuting corruption in the private sector. Subject to parliamentary approval, Bangladesh would join the Open Government Partnership.

Although income tax returns are private documents, BNP proposed allowing the Anti-Corruption Commission or another authorised body to summon them through the court.

The party also pledged to form an independent inquiry commission to identify officials involved in state terror and repression during the July uprising, and to punish officials found responsible for vote rigging and corruption.

It further promised legal and constitutional protection for those who participated in the historic July student-mass uprising of 2024.

Nahid called on the authorities to disclose the whereabouts of protest organisers and the legal grounds for their detention, respect the right to peaceful assembly, and allow journalists to report without intimidation or seizure of equipment.

“From Dhaka, we stand with you as friends bound by a common demand for accountable power, democratic institutions, and human dignity,” the NCP leader said in a statement titled “Statement of Solidarity with the Youth of India”, posted on his Facebook account.

The statement expressed concern over the detention of protesters and journalists in New Delhi, as well as internet suspension and restrictions around Jantar Mantar.

Today, Indian police detained hundreds of demonstrators amid a crackdown on a planned protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in voter list revisions. Delhi Police said the rally had not been authorised.

Drawing parallels with Bangladesh’s July 2024 uprising, Nahid recalled how protests over public service job quotas grew into a nationwide movement against the then Awami League government.

“Hindutva majoritarianism, fascism, and every form of religious supremacy must not define the future of South Asia,” the statement said, calling for greater communal harmony, social justice and protection of minority rights.

Nahid said the struggles of people in the two countries were also linked to unresolved issues involving border killings, water sharing, environmental protection and national sovereignty.

He called for a South Asia where countries treat one another as equals and governments remain accountable.

“The government’s job is not to sleep. The people should sleep peacefully while the government stands guard. A government that cannot give people peace, a government under which people cannot sleep safely, is not needed,” he said.

Shafiqur said while inaugurating a weeklong dengue-prevention awareness campaign organised by Dhaka north city Jamaat at Madhubagh Field in Dhaka’s Hatirjheel.

Jamaat will observe the campaign nationwide till October 10.

Shafiqur said his party had a responsibility towards the country despite being in the opposition.

“Akhtaruzzaman spoke for the victims and expatriate Bangladeshis who keep the wheels of the country’s economy moving,” he said.

Photo: Saurav Hossain Siam At least 10 people were injured in a clash between local activists of Awami League, whose activities remain banned, and BNP, allegedly over control of the brick kiln business in Fatullah, Narayanganj.

The clash broke out around 12:00pm today in Akbarnagar village under Baktaboli union, said Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime) Tarek Al Mehedi.

At 6:00pm, members of both groups were still positioned on opposite sides, the police officer said. Additional police personnel and members of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) were deployed to bring the situation under control.

According to police and local residents, the clash involved activists loyal to Samed Ali, a union Awami League activist, and those aligned with Halim Azad, organising secretary of the Baktaboli union BNP. The two sides had been at odds over establishing local dominance and controlling the supply of labour and soil to brick kilns along the Dhaleshwari river.

Witnesses said the Baktaboli union Jatiyatabadi Krishak Dal organised a programme against drugs, terrorism and extortion this morning in Char Baktaboli, a village next to Akbarnagar.

Halim and other leaders of the BNP and its affiliated organisations attended the meeting as guests.

Later, around noon, Halim and his followers staged a procession in front of Samed’s house in Akbarnagar. A clash then broke out between them and Samed's followers, witnesses said.

Samed's younger son, Md Hridoy, 26, suffered gunshot wounds on his leg in the incident. He was given first aid at Narayanganj 300-bed Hospital and referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), said Dr Apu Kumar Saha, an emergency medical officer at the Narayanganj hospital.

Another youth, Raju Sheikh, 30, of Baktaboli union, was brought to the same hospital with wounds in his leg. He was also advised to go to DMCH.

At least eight others, including Shamsul, 32, of Akbarnagar and Sourav, 28, of Madhyanagar, were injured. They received treatment at local hospitals.

Hridoy alleged that Halim's followers attacked him as he was leaving home for his business establishment.

“His men fired indiscriminately,” Hridoy said.

Halim said, “After the programme, as we were returning, Samed Ali's men attacked our leaders and activists. Samed Ali is a leader of the Awami League and an accused in a murder case related to the anti-discrimination movement. Yet his men continue to extort money at the brick kilns. We want extortion to stop. We do not support any attack.”

Meanwhile, family members of Samed Ali alleged that BNP activists vandalised his house around 3:00pm today, following the clash.

“After August [2024], BNP men took over all our businesses. Halim and his men want to remove us and take control of everything,” Samed said.

Additional Superintendent of Police (A Circle) Shamim Hossain, who was at the site, said the situation in Akbarnagar was brought under control by 6:20pm.

“We have arrested two people in connection with the clash and seized some teta (locally made sharp weapon). Our operation is continuing,” he said.

The arrestee was identified as Abdus Salam, 56, said Gaziur Rahman, spokesperson for Rajshahi Metropolitan Police.

Mizanur Rahman, president of Rajpara Thana BNP, confirmed to The Daily Star yesterday that Salam is the vice-president of the thana BNP unit.

He confirmed that Salam was present at the scene, along with some other BNP men, adding that their actions had now created trouble for the party.

The arrest came after Nazmul Hossain, personal secretary to the RMU vice-chancellor, filed a case with Rajpara Police Station on Tuesday night, against 50 to 60 unidentified persons. Police said the case was recorded the same night.

A group of 20 to 50 people allegedly stormed the VC’s office around Thursday noon, while Prof Jawadul Haque was attending a virtual meeting with health ministry officials on ongoing construction projects.

RMU Deputy Registrar Md Mofakkharul Islam said the group ordered the VC to sign a resignation letter “without reading it”. When the VC’s personal secretary, Nazmul Hossain, intervened, he was assaulted and later allegedly forced to sign a separate resignation letter, despite telling the group he was a regular employee.

The group allegedly took both resignation letters, along with the VC’s mobile phone and laptop. University officials later found that CCTV equipment had been removed, electricity, internet and other communication services disconnected, and several rooms locked, disrupting regular university activities.

Prof Jawadul Haque told The Daily Star that some of those who entered his office appeared linked to local contractors, while others were outsiders allegedly backed by political groups. He said they accused him of awarding university contracts to Dhaka-based firms instead of local contractors, and chanted slogans branding him an “Awami League collaborator”.

“The election is only one step,” said Riaz, distinguished professor of politics and government at Illinois State University.

He said the latest political transition would depend on whether institutions such as the Election Commission, Anti-Corruption Commission, judiciary and civil administration could function independently.

He was speaking at a session titled “Can Bangladesh Break the Cycle?” at the Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026 in Dhaka.

He said Bangladesh had repeatedly failed to build institutions capable of sustaining democracy, with power remaining concentrated and anti-reform forces entrenched within the system.

He said the problem went beyond political interference in the bureaucracy, as successive governments sought a subservient administration, while some bureaucrats were also willing to become politicised.

He described the 2024 uprising as “a rejection of the political parties in this country”, but said political parties later “recaptured the space”.

Asked whether Bangladesh could break the cycle, Riaz said it was too early to conclude that it could not.

“I am optimistic,” he said, adding that the outcome would depend on whether political forces were willing to change the system.

He said Bangladesh needed an independent judiciary and Election Commission, as well as constitutional and institutional changes to address the concentration of power in the executive.

Riaz also cited Bangladesh’s geopolitical position as a challenge for the next government, particularly its relations with India and the wider strategic competition involving India, China and the United States.

Sreeradha Dutta, professor at OP Jindal Global University, India, and Michael Lidauer, senior international adviser at the European Partnership for Democracy, Germany, also spoke at the session.

The assurance came during a meeting with leaders of the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) at the official residence of the leader of the opposition on Minto Road in Dhaka today, according to a press release.

The meeting discussed incentives for the textile sector, gas and power supply, challenges arising from Bangladesh's graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category, taxes, duties and various policy issues.

At a briefing after the meeting, Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar said the party did not believe in opposing every government initiative.

“They want to play the role of a constructive opposition,” he said, quoting Shafiqur Rahman. He added that Jamaat would support government initiatives serving public and national interests while criticising and protesting policies that go against those interests.

According to the press release, BTMA leaders highlighted a range of challenges facing the textile sector.

Shafiqur stressed the importance of ensuring raw material supply for export-oriented industries, protecting the domestic primary textile sector, increasing local value addition, safeguarding employment and conserving foreign currency.

The meeting also discussed protecting government revenue, preventing misuse of bonded warehouse facilities and curbing illegal imports, the release said.

BTMA Vice-President Shafiqul Islam Sarker said the sector had around $32 billion in investment and serves as a key backward linkage industry for the country's apparel sector.

Although gas and power supplies have improved to some extent, many factories continue to face difficulties, he said.

Porwar said BTMA leaders' concerns had been taken seriously and reiterated that the issues would be raised in parliament and discussed with the government in the interests of the economy and the public.

Meanwhile, asked about the reported departure from the longstanding practice of having the leader of the opposition as chief guest at the closing ceremony of the textile and apparel fair Batexpo on November 18, Porwar said there had traditionally been a practice of having the prime minister as chief guest at the opening and the leader of the opposition at the closing.

He said the practice reflected democratic political culture and mutual respect among state institutions. However, he added that Shafiqur Rahman had neither demanded nor requested to be made chief guest.

BTMA President Showkat Aziz Russell, Vice-President Shafiqul Islam Sarker and other directors attended the meeting. Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair and Central Executive Council members, including Mobarak Hossain, Nurul Islam Bulbul, and Md Selim Uddin, were also present.

The party's top leaders also expressed concern over rising prices of essential goods and the hardship faced by ordinary people. They discussed stronger market monitoring and action against syndicates to bring prices under control.

The issues were discussed during a meeting of the BNP National Standing Committee at the party chairman's office on Saturday evening. Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman chaired the meeting.

According to participants, BNP leaders reviewed security arrangements and preparations for the festival across the country. They urged grassroots activists to support the Hindu community, volunteer at puja venues and avoid provocative behaviour or anything that could lead to tension.

A standing committee member, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the discussion focused on preventing people with ulterior motives from causing trouble during the celebrations. The leader said the government would take precautionary measures to maintain law and order, while party members would cooperate with the authorities.

Speaking after the meeting, BNP Acting Secretary General and Prime Minister's Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said the main focus was how to share the joy of Puja with everyone.

Party volunteers would coordinate with local puja committees at venues across the country, he said.

Rizvi also alleged that certain groups were spreading propaganda and plotting against the country and its democratic government. He said the government would counter such efforts and urged party members to stay vigilant.

To oversee the festival, the BNP formed a 12-member central monitoring committee on October 9.

The standing committee discussed the rising cost of daily essentials and its impact on households. Sources said leaders called for tighter market supervision, action against syndicates and more effective steps by the authorities to ease pressure on consumers.

They also discussed the banking sector, remittance inflows and ways to revive wider economic activity.

The growing drug problem was another concern, with leaders calling for tougher measures to protect young people. They also stressed better waste management and a stronger response from local government bodies to contain dengue.

Other topics included the prime minister's participation in the UN General Assembly, his Japan visit, opposition parties' activities and the BNP's organisational affairs.

Meeting sources said preparations for local government elections were discussed. Asked about the BNP's national council or restructuring party committees, Rizvi said organisational matters had come up but he had no decision or message to announce.

Tarique calls BNP’s parliamentary party meeting

Leader of the House Tarique Rahman has called a meeting of the BNP parliamentary party at 6:00pm today (Sunday) in the ruling party's meeting room at the Jatiya Sangsad.

The move is unusual because parliamentary party meetings are generally held shortly before a House session or while parliament is sitting. The next session has yet to be scheduled; it may begin in the second week of November.

Several senior BNP leaders said the meeting could address party discipline, law and order, constitutional amendments, local government elections and other political and organisational challenges. They believe the prime minister may want to give lawmakers guidance on urgent issues.

A senior BNP leader told The Daily Star on condition of anonymity, "The prime minister has called everyone. He will certainly give instructions on some important and urgent matters."

One pressing issue is the series of allegations of land grabbing, extortion and other irregularities involving party members.

A recent example is the attack and vandalism at the Radda healthcare centre in Mirpur.

Following the incident, Ferdousy Ahmed, a BNP MP from a reserved women's seat, resigned. Allegations against her remain under investigation. The party also dissolved three committees, including its Dhaka Metropolitan North unit, and expelled 14 leaders and activists at different levels.

The episode has raised questions about the conduct of people linked to local party politics and how quickly the leadership responds when serious complaints emerge.

Those steps signalled that the leadership was prepared to act against people accused of using the party's name for grabbing property, extortion or violence.

The coming local government elections pose another test. After the national polls, BNP leaders must manage expectations of grassroots members, competition among prospective candidates and disagreements over nominations while identifying candidates acceptable to voters.

Senior leaders are expected to consider how the party can maintain order in local units as activists and prospective candidates seek a larger role.

With the election timetable still uncertain, instructions from the centre could influence how local units prepare.

Sources also expect discussion of organisational discipline, the restructuring of party bodies and decisions on committees whose terms have expired.

National reconciliation without justice is not peace but “simply a pause between conflicts”, he said while speaking at a session titled “Justice, Accountability, and National Reconciliation” at the Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026 in Dhaka.

He said transition from autocracy to democracy is often threatened by institutional remnants of former regimes.

“Transitional justice requires far more than symbolic gestures or premature calls for unity. It demands forensic, systemic dismantling of impunity,” he said.

He said reconciliation had at times been used around the world as a political shield to protect perpetrators of state violence from legal consequences.

Referring to Bangladesh’s political transition following the July-August uprising of 2024, the deputy speaker said the events culminating on August 5 represented more than a change of government.

“What occurred leading up to and on the 5th of August was not merely a change of administration. It was fundamentally redefining our political paradigm,” he said.

Those responsible for abuses under the previous government must be brought to justice, he said, arguing that accountability was necessary not only as punishment but also to prevent authoritarian rule from recurring.

Kayser Kamal rejected calls from some quarters at home and abroad for reconciliation with the former regime.

“Their criminal, inhuman and ruthless actions against their own citizens have permanently disqualified them from any role in our political future,” he said.

“One cannot reconcile with an apparatus that systematically weaponised the state against the very people it was supposed to protect,” he added.

Kayser Kamal also said the post-August government must remain subject to accountability and public scrutiny.

“A government’s legitimacy is derived solely from its transparency and its willingness to subject itself to relentless public scrutiny,” he said.

Justice mechanisms, he said, must operate independently of political influence, while institutions should serve as custodians of the people’s will rather than instruments of those in power.

New Age Editor Nurul Kabir, speaking at the session, said genuine reconciliation required three elements: a shared investigation into the conflict, reparations for victims, and admission of guilt and punishment of perpetrators.

“After these three things are over, a genuine reconciliation can start,” he said.

He said conflict and confrontation were not inherently negative, citing anti-colonial struggles through which many societies secured political independence. But conflicts within nation states eventually required processes to establish responsibility and enable societies to move towards reconciliation.

He cited Northern Ireland, Colombia and South Africa as examples of efforts to develop frameworks for resolving prolonged conflicts.

In Bangladesh, Nurul Kabir identified three major unresolved areas of confrontation: the legacy of the 1971 Liberation War, the conflict in the Chittagong Hill Tracts and the violence surrounding the 2024 uprising.

On 1971, he said those who collaborated with Pakistani forces had yet to acknowledge their role and admit guilt, adding that many of them were now organised under the banner of Jamaat-e-Islami.

On the Chittagong Hill Tracts, he said reconciliation required both Bengali and non-Bengali communities to recognise their mistakes and jointly assess responsibility for the prolonged conflict.

Referring to the 2024 uprising, Nurul Kabir said he had yet to see remorse from those responsible for killing pro-democracy protesters.

“They are rather still blaming or accusing millions of protesters who took to the streets in July and August 2024,” he said.

Nurul Kabir said reconciliation cannot begin until those responsible for wrongdoing recognised their actions and accepted accountability.

Karori Singh, professor at the University of Rajasthan, said public office should be treated as a position of trust and adequate safeguards were needed to prevent office-holders from exercising arbitrary power.

Madalitso Zililo Phiri, a researcher at Wits University in South Africa, said debates on justice and reconciliation also needed to address structural inequalities inherited from the past, including those based on race, geography, ethnicity and gender.

Drawing on Cambodia’s experience, Nikki Singer, executive director of the Centre for Peace and Conflict Studies, said reconciliation could continue for decades after formal conflict ended.

She stressed the importance of narratives, dialogue and how societies remembered the past, while cautioning that an exclusive focus on assigning blame could make it difficult for societies to move forward.

title: OC in trouble for demanding biriyani, sweets
body:
Shayestaganj Police Station officer-in-charge (OC) has been accused of sending letters to three local companies demanding food items worth over Tk 10 lakh to entertain guests invited on the occasion of Police Day and Durga Puja.

The Habiganj district police formed a committee to investigate the allegation last night after learning of the matter from police officials, local media outlets, and social media, Habiganj Additional Superintendent of Police Khalilur Rahman told our Moulvibazar correspondent this morning.

Sheikh Nazmul Kamal requested food items worth Tk 3.5 lakh from each of the three companies via letters delivered by his constables.

Each letter asked for 300 plates of biryani, 30kg of jilapi, 30kg of sweets, 300 packets of curd, and 500 bottles of water, Khalilur added.

The committee is headed by ASP Samshul Haque and the other members are ASP Khalilur and Special Branch Inspector Rafiqul Islam. They will submit the probe report within three working days.

The letters were addressed to the managing director of Square Denims Ltd in Olipur, the MD of Tafrid Cotton Mills in the same area, and the general manager (administration) of PRAN-RFL Group at Habiganj Industrial Park.

Contacted, Touhiduzzaman, assistant general manager (PR) at PRAN-RFL Group, confirmed that they had received the letter.

This correspondent tried to contact OC Kamal for his comment on the allegation, but he did not pick up the phone despite multiple calls.
summary: Shayestaganj OC accused of demanding food items worth over Tk 10 lakh from 3 companies to entertain guests invited on the occasion of Police Day and Durga Puja

title: Water scarcity hampers jute processing
body:
High yield of jute fails to make farmers in Faridpur happy as they are facing huge trouble to rot and process raw jute in absence of adequate water in local water bodies (Beels), canals and ponds.

Farmers said if the ongoing water crisis continues, they will have to count huge loss this year as quality fibres cannot be extracted without properly rotting.

According to Faridpur Department of Agriculture Extension (DAE), jute was cultivated on 85, 865 hectares of land in nine upazila of the district while it was cultivated to 85,201 hectares last year.

Many farmers said raw jute processing has been badly hampered as they cannot rot their jute plants due to lack of rain water even in the middle of monsoon.

Moreover, they have to spend additional labour cost for carrying the jute plants to other place for rotting, farmers said, adding that this year day labourers are charging Tk 550 to Tk 600, which is Tk 150 to Tk 200 more compared to the previous year.

While visiting different villages in Nagarkanda and Saltha upazilas this correspondent saw piled up jute stalks are drying up on the field as there is no water to process those.

Meanwhile, some farmers were seen carrying their jute plants to other places for processing.

Farmer Sarwar Matubbar of Salitha village in Nagarkanda upazila said he cultivated jute on four bighas of land this year, spending Tk 60,000.

But due to lack of adequate water he couldn't rot half of his jute plants on two bighas, Sarwar added.

Another jute grower Haridas Biswas of Boutipara village in the upazila said every year they have to cut the jute plants a bit early as rain water starts entering their field.

"But the situation is different this season," he said.

Farmer Abdul Gaffar of Ramkantapur in Saltha upazila said he cultivated jute on three bighas of land and had already sold 4.5 maunds of raw jute at Tk 3,000 per maund.

"I have cut the rest of the jute plant in last few days, but could not rot those due to lack of adequate water," Gaffar said.

Shajahan Sheikh of Chhoto Bahirdia village in the upazila said usually farmers sow jute seeds at the end of March and complete the harvesting by last week of June every year. Faridpur DAE Deputy Director Hazrat Ali said jute plants are getting dried up as jute growers in all the upazilas of the district are facing serious problem in processing jute plants due to lack of rain water this season.
summary: High yield of jute fails to make farmers in Faridpur happy as they are facing huge trouble to rot and process raw jute in absence of adequate water in local water bodies (Beels), canals and ponds.

title: Auto rice mill near school
body:
An influential quarter is setting up an auto rice mill close to a government primary school at Atharodana in Ghatail upazila, ignoring local people's objection.

Villagers said if the rice mill near Atharodana Badeparshi Government Primary School goes into operation, it will destroy local environment and pose health risk to the students and teachers of the educational institution.

Meanwhile, agitated locals staged a demonstration recently and demanded to stop the ongoing construction of the rice mill there.

Local administration, however, could not stop the construction work as the owner of the mill got approval from the Directorate of Environment (DoE).

Locals said construction of Dhaleshwari Agro Food Mills, which is only a few hundred feet away from Atharodana Badeparshi Government Primary School, started in October last year.

They also submitted a complaint to the local administration and DoE in this regard, but to no effect, villagers further said.

A number of guardians including Anwarul Kabir and Azmat Ali said if the mill is constructed there it will badly hamper the kids' education.

"If the mill is constructed beside the school, I will have to shift my son to other school," Anwarul said.

Headmaster of Atharodana Badeparshi Government Primary School Khorshed Alam said although they raised their objection against the construction of the rice mill, the owner did not bother.

Contacted, Anwar Hossain, owner of the under-construction rice mill, said before the start of the mill construction work, an advertisement was published in the newspapers, saying if anyone has any objection in this regard, but no one raised any objection then.

Later, I got approval from the DoE, he said, adding that although construction of another mill is going on some distance away, a section people is instigating the villagers to raise objection against his mill.

When asked about the environment pollution, Anwar said now everything is automated.

Because of using modern technologies, it will pose no threat to local people and the school kids, the further said.

Ghatail Upazila Education Officer Masudur Rahman said although investigations had been conducted in this regard on several occasions, the construction work is still going on.

Ghatail Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Munia Chowdhury said the mill owner has valid approval from the DoE.

Md Ziaul Haque, director of DoE (Dhaka region), said they held three hearings in this regard. Although the mill owner appeared in the hearing, the school authorities did not, he added.
summary: An influential quarter is setting up an auto rice mill close to a government primary school at Atharodana in Ghatail upazila, ignoring local people’s objection.

title: Ramshackle ratnai bridge: An impediment of development
body:
Economic activities in four upazilas including three in Kurigram district and one in Lalmonirhat could not gain the momentum as desired despite the inauguration of the Sheikh Hasina Dharla Bridge over the Dharla river in 2018.

The Bailey bridge over the Ratnai river in Kulaghat area of Lalmonirhat Sadar upazila, the doorway of the newly-built Dharla Bridge on Lalmonirhat- Phulbari road is vulnerable and narrow and may collapse anytime.

Local business people and traders said that the business as well as development activities in the region especially in Phulbari, Nageshwari and Bhurungamari upazilas of Kurigram and Lalmonirhat Sadar upazila could not pick up the pace due to the ramshackle Bailey bridge over the river Ratnai.

The derelict bridge remains an obstacle to the movement of larger transports and cargo vehicles on the road connecting Lalmonirhat with Kurigram and other parts of the country, they also said.

Sahidur Rahman, a businessman from Phulbari upazila in Kurigram, said that they were unable to take the advantage of the new Dharla bridge as the narrow Bailey bridge on Ratnai stands in the way of transporting larger payloads.

"Due to the precarious and narrow Bailey bridge over Ratnai, we are deprived of the benefits of the newly-built Dharla Bridge," he said.

To expedite the socio-economic development in the region, the new Dharla bridge -- built at a cost of Tk 206 crore and 85 lakh -- has to be used to its full potential, said Moktarul Islam, another businessman from the same upazila.

To achieve that objective, the Bailey bridge over the river Ratnai needs to be replaced with a stronger and wider bridge as soon as possible, he also said.

Echoing the same, Sheikh Abdul Hamid Babu, president of the Chambers of Commerce and Industries in Lalmonirhat, said he has been pursuing the Roads and Highways Department (RHD) for a new bridge on the Ratnai, but his efforts so have far borne no result.

"If a new bridge is built replacing the vulnerable Bailey bridge over Ratnai River, it will tremendously benefit us," he said.

Executive Engineer of RHD in Lalmonirhat Khalid Saifullah said a tender will be invited soon for constructing the 138.44-metre long and 10.25-metre-wide concrete bridge replacing the Bailey bridge over the Ratnai river at a cost of Tk 36 crore.

"The work for constructing the new bridge will start in September this year," he hoped.
summary: Economic activities in four upazilas including three in Kurigram district and one in Lalmonirhat could not gain the momentum as desired despite the inauguration of the Sheikh Hasina Dharla Bridge over the Dharla river in 2018.

title: Sudden Jamuna erosion makes many homeless
body:
Sudden erosion by the Jamuna river has devoured several homesteads and vast farmlands within a few hours at Mazzan village in Sirajganj's Shahzadpur upazila last week, creating panic among the villagers.

"As I came to know that sudden erosion by the Jamuna started eroding a portion the riverbank in our village, I rushed to my house, but unfortunately couldn't save anything," Rafikul Islam of Mazzan village said.

"When I reached home, I saw it was already on the verge of being eroded, but I didn't dare to go inside," Rafikul said, adding that I lost my homestead, cultivable land and a happy family within few minutes last Friday.

"Two of my four children were playing at the courtyard when my house was devouring. I somehow managed to save my kids, nothing else as the entire house washed away into the river in front of my eyes," another erosion-hit victim Rozina Khatun said.

"Now me and my four children are living in a roadside makeshift shanty, but I have nothing to feed my family as all our food grains, stocked at the house, also went into the river last week," Rozina further said.

Affected villagers said due to the sudden erosion at least 13 houses went into river while another 20 to 25 shifted to other places in last one week.

Sirajganj Water Development Board (WDB) Executive Engineer Shafikul Islam said due to geographical state of the Jamuna erosion is a common catastrophe in Sirajganj during flood.

WDB has already took up a mega project of Tk 600 crore to protect 6.5-kilometre portion of the flood protection embankment in a bid to save Enayetpur, Shahzadpur and Belkuchi upazilas from further erosion, the WDB engineer said.

According to Sirajganj district administration so far around 974 homesteads, at different villages in five upazilas of the district, devoured in the Jamuna during the ongoing flood and the affected villagers need urgent rehabilitation.
summary: Sudden erosion by the Jamuna river has devoured several homesteads and vast farmlands within a few hours at Mazzan village in Sirajganj’s Shahzadpur upazila last week, creating panic among the villagers.

title: Natore UP member found dead, wife injured
body:
Police recovered the body of a local union parishad (UP) member from his second wife's house at Joanpur in Naldanga upazila early yesterday.

The deceased, Abdul Alim, 40, a member of Ward No 1 under Madhanagar UP, was son of late Ashraful Islam of West Madhanagar village in the upazila.

The law enforcers also rescued Alim's second wife Rima Begum, who sustained stab injuries, and admitted her to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital.

Madhanagar UP Chairman Abdul Jabbar said Alim went to his second wife Rima's house on Monday evening.

After having their dinner, the couple locked in a quarrel over different family issues at the dead of night.

Later, hearing Rima's screams, her mother Eleka Begum entered the room and found the duo lying in the floor unconscious and informed the police, he said.

Being informed, Naldanga police recovered Alim's body and sent it to the hospital morgue for autopsy.

Deceased's younger brother Ashiq Ali alleged that his brother was killed in a planned manner and demanded proper investigation in this regard.

Officer in Charge of Naldanga Police Station Shafiqul Islam said the reason behind the death will be clear once the autopsy is done.
summary: Police recovered the body of a local union parishad (UP) member from his second wife’s house at Joanpur in Naldanga upazila early yesterday.

title: Two kids drown in Lalmonirhat, Kurigram
body:
Two children died in separate incidents of drowning in Lalmonirhat and Kurigram on Monday.

The deceased are Abdur Rahman, 7, son of Shafiqul Islam of Ramna village in Kurigram's Chilmari upazila, and Nirmal Chandra, 4, son of Khitish Chandra of Bhatibari village in Lalmonirhat Sadar upazila.

Quoting the deceased's family members, police said, Rahman, a Class I student at Ramna Govt Primary School, drowned while he was fishing in a waterbody (Beel) nearby his house.

Meanwhile, Nirmal died when he fell into the water while playing beside a pond adjacent to his house.

Hearing screams, villagers rescued the boy and took him to the hospital where the doctors declared him dead.
summary: Two children died in separate incidents of drowning in Lalmonirhat and Kurigram on Monday.

title: Permanent shops on leased land!
body:
Violating rules and without taking permission from the authorities concerned a local influential man has been constructing permanent shops after taking lease of a rural market at Dhalapara in Ghatail upazila.

Moreover, the lease holder evicted the former traders, who had been running their business for long, and allocating the newly-constructed shops to others in exchange of huge money, evicted traders alleged.

The influential leaseholder, backed by powerful political quarters and a section of local public representatives, allegedly realizing Tk 5 to Tk 6 lakh for allocating each shop to the other people, they said.

As a result, nearly 300 small traders, who had been holding business on the rural market, became unemployed.

Finding no other alternative, the aggrieved traders submitted a written complaint to the local upazila nirbahi officer (UNO) recently, but yet to get any solution in this regard.

Shafiqul Islam, who was the previous lease holder, took lease of the traditional Dhalapara market this year at a cost of Tk 20.71 lakh.

But surprisingly, soon after taking lease of the market this year, Shafiqul evicted the former traders from their allocated places, saying some new shops will be constructed in front of the market.

Usually, a small space (viti) of the rural market is allocate to traders in exchange of a small amount of revenue every year, but the scenario is different this year, traders alleged.

They said leaseholder Shafiqul has already constructed a number of permanent shops, including 48 in front of the playground of a local school and a pond, on the leased market.

He later started allocating those shops to other traders in exchange of huge money, depriving the previous small traders, they further said.

Asked about the matter, Abdul Awal, a land official (Nayeb) at Dhalapara Union Land Office, said Shafiqul got the lease of the market for one year and he didn't know anything about construction of any shops there.

Contacted, Shafiqul said after getting lease of the market this year he has constructed some new shops there.

In an interview with a private TV channel, Tangail Deputy Commissioner Dr Ataul Gani said construction of permanent structures or shops on any leased rural market is a complete violation of rules.

After investigation, necessary steps will be taken in this regard, he added.
summary: Violating rules and without taking permission from the authorities concerned a local influential man has been constructing permanent shops after taking lease of a rural market at Dhalapara in Ghatail upazila.

title: Illegal pond:  A threat to surrounding cropland
body:
A local Awami League (AL) leader has dug a pond illegally posing threats to the surrounding cropland and homesteads. An act that he has done after failing to buy the villagers' land at a cheap rate, locals said.

Aminul Islam is the general secretary of Durgapur union unit of AL in Lalmonirhat's Aditmari upazila.

Union Assistant Land Officer Abdul Hamid has filed a case against Aminul with Aditmari Police Station under the Sand Mahal and Land Management Act 2010.

According to what could be known, Aminul wanted to buy cultivable land and homesteads of eight villagers at a cheap rate. However, as the villagers refused his offer, he started digging a pond on his eight bighas of land illegally posing threats to surrounding cropland and homesteads, inhabitants of Dwarkuti village said.

Around one kilometre stretch of the dirt road in the village is now in an impassable state due to transporting earth and sand from the pond. The village graveyard lying on the bank of the pond is also at the risk of being devoured.

Mostafa Ali, 55, a farmer from Dwarkuti village, said his farmland was being devoured by the illegally excavated pond and his homestead was also under threat.

"AL man Aminul Islam proposed me that I sell my land to him and move to somewhere else. But I didn't agree to it. Now, I am losing my arable land and homestead," he said.

Contacted, Aminul Islam said that he was digging a pond on his own land and it matters little to him whose land and homesteads being devoured.

However, he denied the allegations that he had offered to buy land at low prices.

Rafiqul Alam, general secretary of Aditmari upazila AL, said Aminul deserves to be punished. Aditmari Upazila Nirbahi Officer GR Sarwar said according to the law, no one can dig a pond and extract sand without permission. A case has been filed against Aminul Islam.
summary: A local Awami League (AL) leader has dug a pond illegally posing threats to the surrounding cropland and homesteads. An act that he has done after failing to buy the villagers’ land at a cheap rate, locals said.

title: Payra erosion threatens Barguna villages
body:
Thousands of villagers in Barguna's Taltali and Amtali upazilas are worried about losing their belongings to continuous erosion of Payra river. The erosion has taken a serious turn recently posing threats to six villages in the upazilas.

The affected villages are Tetulbaria, Sobahanpara, Ankujanpara and Jayalbhanga in Taltali upazila and Baliatali and Baithakata in Amtali upazila.

According to the locals, the flood control dyke at Tetulbaria village in Taltali upazila has collapsed recently exacerbating the flood situation.

The inhabitants of Sobahanpara, Ankujanpara and Jayalbhanga villages are spending sleepless nights in fear of erosion.

Fear of losing all their belongings has gripped around 10,000 people of these villages.

Locals said that after the devastating cyclone Sidr in 2007, the dyke has not been repaired much. At least 3,000 people of these areas have been rendered homeless and they have been relocated to Barguna, Barishal and Dhaka.

Emadul, a victim of river erosion of Tetulbaria village, said that he has lost three bighas of land to an eroding Payra. He has also lost his house to erosion.

Fisherman Hamed Ali said, "All of my lands except my dwelling house have been washed away by the river."

"Where will I stand with my family if I lose the shelter?," he questioned.

On the other hand, about 500 metre stretch of the flood control dyke at Baliatali village in Amtali upazila has been damaged due to erosion of Payra.

Although a ring dam was built here by Water Development Board (WDB) last year, it is now under threat of erosion, villagers said.

Barguna Water Development Board Executive Engineer Nurul Islam said necessary steps will be taken to curb erosion at Jayal Bhanga point in Taltali and Tetulbaria village. Proposals have been sent to the higher authorities to prevent further erosion in Baithakata and Baliatali villages.
summary: Thousands of villagers in Barguna’s Taltali and Amtali upazilas are worried about losing their belongings to continuous erosion of Payra river. The erosion has taken a serious turn recently posing threats to six villages in the upazilas.

title: Ensure justice for child abuse, not mob justice: Hefazat
body:
Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh has called for exemplary punishment through fair investigations into allegations of child abuse and misconduct at educational institutions, saying that neither such acts nor taking the law into one's own hands is acceptable.

In a statement sent to the media today, Hefazat Ameer Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Sajedur Rahman made the call.

They said ensuring exemplary punishment through proper investigations and administrative measures was crucial for the sake of maintaining law and order in the country.

Describing child sexual abuse as a longstanding social problem, the Hefazat leaders said this is not an issue specific to any particular community. Such incidents occur to varying degrees across different sectors, including schools and madrasas, they added.

The statement said Al-Haiatul Ulya Lil-Jamiatil Qawmia Bangladesh issued new directives on September 19 for the country's six Qawmi madrasa boards and their affiliated institutions to prevent student abuse.

Under the directives, every madrasa must form “a student protection committee” or reactivate an existing one. Complaints of student abuse or misconduct must be investigated and reports submitted within seven days.

The madrasa boards have also been instructed to establish strong monitoring cells and launch hotlines to receive complaints.

The statement warned that if any madrasa lacked a student protection committee, the committee remained inactive, or the institution failed to act on complaints, the affiliation of the madrasa could be postponed or cancelled.

The Hefazat leaders said the safety and psychological well-being of children must always be prioritised at educational institutions. For this, schools and madrasas must adopt strict policies and ensure round-the-clock monitoring through CCTV cameras, they added.

They urged all schools and madrasas to follow the directives issued by their respective higher authorities.

Those found guilty of misconduct must face both institutional and legal action, the statement said, adding that there should be no leniency or compromise in such cases.

The leaders stressed that no compromises can be made regarding the responsibility to ensure a safe environment and quality education for children.
summary: Calls for fair investigations, exemplary punishment and stronger child protection measures at schools and madrasas

title: Home minister busy with every ministry but his own: Shafiqur
body:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman has criticised Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed for interfering in the affairs of other ministries while failing to manage his own ministry and maintain law and order in the country.

"Fortunately, we got such a home minister. He serves in all ministries. He neither controlled drugs nor weapons, nor was he able to restore law and order in the country,” he said while speaking to journalists at Moulvibazar Circuit House in the morning

It was his first organisational visit in his home district of Moulvibazar since the national elections.

Shafiqur said the home ministry is the most sensitive and critical ministry in any state, and a properly functioning home ministry is essential to maintaining law and order in the country. However, he alleged that the current home minister failed to manage his own ministry and was interfering in the affairs of others -- including education, health and local government. Such interference, he said, was not a hallmark of good governance.

Expressing concern, the opposition leader said there was effectively no law and order in the country. Incidents of murder, rape, extortion and illegal land grabbing were increasing daily.

He alleged that the police administration was being used for partisan purposes, saying police should serve as friends of the public rather than as henchmen of any political party. The reality, he said, was the opposite.

Shafiqur also spoke strongly against corruption and extortion, saying those involved in such activities did not truly belong to any political party and brought ruin upon themselves and their parties. When a party faced a crisis, such people were the first to flee.

He said there was no place for corrupt individuals or extortionists in Jamaat-e-Islami. Urging party leaders and activists to remain alert, he added that many people previously involved in looting and extortion were now trying to seek refuge in different political parties.

Those who plunder public resources should not be considered patriots, he said, adding that they would ultimately face judgment in the “court of the people”.

On the development of Moulvibazar, he said the district remained underdeveloped despite having a significant tea industry and a large expatriate community.

He pledged to play an active role in the parliament to push for improvements in the district’s infrastructure, educational institutions, and healthcare services.
summary: Police administration being used for partisan purposes, says Shafiqur

title: Police file GD over Rumeen Farhana-Sarail OC confrontation
body:
Police have lodged a general diary (GD) over an altercation between independent lawmaker Rumeen Farhana and Sarail Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Manzur Kader Bhuiyan.

The GD was filed at Sarail Police Station on Thursday night, but the development came to light yesterday (Friday) evening.

Confirming the matter, OC Manzur Kader said police were preparing a list of those who accompanied the lawmaker at the police station.

Further action would be taken in line with instructions from senior police officials, he added.

Rumeen, who represents Brahmanbaria-2, comprising Sarail, Ashuganj and part of Bijoynagar, along with her supporters went to the OC's office at around 7:30pm on Thursday. An altercation ensued over alleged security lapses and police misconduct.

Several videos of their heated exchange later circulated on Facebook.

Her supporters said tensions between the MP and the OC had been building over the past few days, alleging that the officer had not responded to calls from the lawmaker and her personal assistant, Zakir Hossain.

They also claimed that Farhana had sought security but did not receive it.

After the incident, Rumeen said she had visited the police station to discuss various allegations against the OC. She said she had brought a two-page list detailing alleged offences by date, but the OC neither commented on the allegations nor provided satisfactory answers.

Meanwhile, her personal assistant Zakir Hossain said they would submit a written complaint against the OC to senior police officials. The process was underway, he added.
summary: Brahmanbaria-2 MP locked horns with OC over security, misconduct on Thursday

title: Govt working to amend various laws, including CSA: minister
body:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Andaleeve Rahman has said the government is working to amend various laws, including the cybersecurity act, to ensure equal protection for all.

He said discussions were underway with stakeholders, including television channel owners and newspaper editors, to make the process more effective.

Policies were being formulated to ensure equal protection for media personnel, the administration and the public, he said, expressing hope for positive results soon.

The minister made the remarks while talking to reporters on Wednesday night during a visit to puja mandaps in his home constituency of Bhola Sadar.

Referring to the killing of a journalist in Netrokona, Andaleeve said any violation of the law, whether involving a journalist or someone from another profession, would be dealt with under existing laws.

The minister visited puja mandaps at nine temples in Bhola Sadar, accompanied by leaders and activists of Bangladesh Jatiya Party (BJP) and its affiliated organisations.
summary: Information and Broadcasting Minister Andaleeve Rahman has said the government is working to amend various laws, including the cybersecurity act, to ensure equal protection for all.

title: No possibility of Hasina’s return in next 10 years: Hafiz
body:
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad yesterday said he believes there is no possibility of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina returning to Bangladesh in the next 10 years.

“From my political experience, I think there is no possibility for Sheikh Hasina to return even in the next 10 years,” he said while talking to reporters at the Bhola Circuit House.

The Speaker said the Awami League, which now faces a ban on its activities, created an environment during its tenure where honest, good and impartial people in society could not contest elections.

He said fundamental reforms to the electoral system are necessary to ensure that ordinary people with public support and social acceptance, even without substantial financial resources, can participate in elections. “The Election Commission should devise a system which will create opportunities for ordinary citizens to contest polls.”

Hafiz Uddin also said the upcoming local government elections must be free, fair and impartial, noting that elections had not been fair over the past 15 years.
summary: Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad yesterday said he believes there is no possibility of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina returning to Bangladesh in the next 10 years.

title: President visits LGRD minister at Evercare Hospital
body:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir yesterday visited Evercare Hospital in the capital to see Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan.

During the visit, the president inquired about the minister’s physical condition and treatment and wished him a speedy recovery, said the President’s Press Wing.

The LGRD minister was admitted to the Evercare Hospital with respiratory and cardiac complications on October 21 and is undergoing treatment there.

Moyeen Khan, also a member of the BNP Standing Committee, is being treated under the supervision of Evercare Hospital physicians Dr Atikur Rahman, Dr Ziaul Haque and Dr Zafar Iqbal.
summary: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir yesterday visited Evercare Hospital in the capital to see Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan.

title: Rumeen locks horns with Sarail OC over security, misconduct
body:
A heated confrontation broke out on Thursday night between Brahmanbaria-2 MP Rumeen Farhana and Sarail Police Station OC Mohammad Monjur Kader Bhuiyan over alleged security lapses and police misconduct.

The incident occurred around 8:00pm at the OC’s office, where local residents accused police of assault, bribery and corruption. Videos of the exchange later circulated on social media.

According to those present, Rumeen alleged that she had been denied personal security while visiting Durga Puja mandaps in Sarail, despite receiving police protection in neighbouring Bijoynagar and Ashuganj upazilas.

She also accused the OC of behaving discourteously towards an elected MP and questioned his alleged political background.

The confrontation intensified when local resident Unda Mia accused the OC of taking Tk 30,000 from him. He alleged that police had assaulted and detained him when he visited the station over a case involving a relative before sending him to court.

Police officers present denied the allegations, while the OC said he did not know the complainant.

Rumeen also accused him of taking money from businesses involved in sand and soil extraction and brick kilns, while maintaining close ties with local Awami League leaders.

The OC rejected the allegations, saying he attended only official state functions. He also questioned claims involving brick kilns, saying many in the area’s haor region remain submerged for part of the year. Several people demanded the OC’s removal and chanted slogans as tensions rose.

Contacted, OC Monjur said Rumeen had arrived with a large group, creating a “mob-like situation”. He claimed the allegations were false and that she had “coached others to make them”.

Regarding her security, he said police had protected her during Durga Puja as part of overall arrangements but lacked the manpower to assign a separate team to accompany her. She needed to apply to the SP’s office for a personal security officer.

Contacted, Rumeen said elected lawmakers are recognised as VIPs under the state’s “Warrant of Precedence” and the administration’s “Red Book”, entitling them to special protocol and security. “However, the Sarail OC did not answer my phone calls. Instead, he said people will provide security to an elected MP. That is why thousands of people have accompanied me. They are providing my security,” she said.

She said she had visited the station to seek clarification about allegations of irregularities and corruption against the OC.
summary: A heated confrontation broke out on Thursday night between Brahmanbaria-2 MP Rumeen Farhana and Sarail Police Station OC Mohammad Monjur Kader Bhuiyan over alleged security lapses and police misconduct.
author: Masuk Hridoy

title: NCP reshuffle: Patwary, Hasnat rise; Samantha, Niva lose senior posts
body:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has restructured its central convening committee, promoting Nasiruddin Patwary, Hasnat Abdullah, and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain while demoting Samantha Sharmin and Nahida Sarwar Niva.

Nahid Islam and Akhter Hossen have retained their positions as convener and member secretary, respectively.

Only two women, Nusrat Tabasum and Mahmuda Mitu, have been included in the party’s 16-member Political Council, its highest policymaking body.

Under the reshuffle announced yesterday, Patwary and Hasnat have been made senior joint conveners, while Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud have become senior joint member secretaries.

Samantha, previously a senior joint convener, has been made a joint convener, while Niva, formerly a senior joint member secretary, has been appointed a joint member secretary.

Both resigned from the party council before the national election in protest against the NCP joining the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance. They remain party members and advisory committee members but have largely been inactive in organisational activities.

The posts of chief coordinator, chief organiser and spokesperson have been abolished.

The Political Council includes Abdullah Al Amin, Atiq Mujahid, Abdul Hannan Masud, Ali Ahsan Junaid, Sarwar Tusher, Saleh Uddin Sifat, Mahmuda Alam Mitu, and Nusrat Tabasum, among others.

Joint Convener Sarwar Tusher said the reshuffle aims to strengthen the party by replacing inactive leaders and bringing district and grassroots leaders into the central committee.

He said those excluded from the committee have been assigned roles in NCP’s front and affiliated organisations, including Chhatra Shakti, Jubo Shakti, Nari Shakti, Sramik Shakti, Olama Alliance, Professionals Alliance, and Private Teachers Alliance.

Two more organisations -- Swechchhasebak Shakti, a front organisation, and the Hindu-Buddhist-Christian Alliance, an affiliated organisation -- are awaiting formal launch, he added.

Tusher said the restructuring aims to strengthen the party’s organisational base ahead of the local government elections.
summary: The National Citizen Party (NCP) has restructured its central convening committee, promoting Nasiruddin Patwary, Hasnat Abdullah, and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain while demoting Samantha Sharmin and Nahida Sarwar Niva.

title: Seven qawmi-based parties: Jamaat suspects govt hand in Hefazat’s unity bid
body:
The initiative to unite seven Islamist political parties under the guidance of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, a Qawmi madrasa-based organisation, could be a ploy to weaken political rivals, Jamaat-e-Islami Assistant Secretary General Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair has alleged.

Referring to recent meetings between Hefazat leaders and the government, Zubair said the possibility of political manoeuvring by the government could not be ruled out.

“Hefazat leaders held discussions with the government. They are not publicly acknowledging it. When the time comes, we will understand what is actually happening,” he told The Daily Star yesterday.

Hefazat, however, says the initiative aims to end divisions among Islamist parties and bring them together, rejecting allegations of government involvement.

At a meeting of the seven parties’ liaison committee at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Makhzanul Ulum madrasa in the capital’s Khilgaon on Thursday, they agreed in principle to work together under the banner of “Like-minded Islamist Parties”.

The parties are Islami Andolan Bangladesh, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh, Khelafat Majlish, Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis, Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan, Islami Oikya Jote and Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party.

At least three of them are partners in the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance.

The meeting discussed the possibility of contesting local government elections jointly, but no decision was made. The parties also failed to reach a consensus on whether members of other political alliances would be required to leave those alliances, said meeting sources.

Zubair said Hefazat could play a role in religious affairs, but if it became involved in politics, it would need to clarify its political position and programmes.

“If the Islamist parties in Bangladesh come together on a single platform, we will be very happy. We have long hoped that all Islamist parties would unite, work together and play a collective role.”

Zubair, however, said Jamaat was not concerned about the potential impact of the new initiative on its 11-party combine and was closely observing developments.

The Jamaat-led alliance was formed ahead of the 12 February national election to build a new Bangladesh through reforms, the Jamaat leader said, adding that their movement for a Bangladesh free from fascism through state and constitutional reforms continued.

The alliance includes Islamist parties, groups involved in the 2024 mass uprising and parties that supported the Liberation War.

WHAT HEFAZAT SAYS

Azizul Haque Islamabadi, joint secretary general of Hefazat-e-Islam, said Islamist parties were split after contesting the last election under different alliances or independently. He added that bringing them together was the initiative’s main objective.

“There is pressure from the public as well as from our leaders and activists to unite the Islamist parties. However, how the parties will proceed ahead of the local government election is their own decision,” he said.

Rejecting the allegations of government involvement, he described them as “unrealistic and baseless”.

Maulana Jalaluddin Ahmad, secretary general of Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis, said the seven parties had decided to coordinate their programmes, statements, and positions on various issues for the welfare of the country, its people, and Islam.

“The decision by these seven parties to work together does not mean that parties belonging to other political alliances will have to leave those alliances. No such decision was made at Thursday’s meeting,” he said.

He added that Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis would remain in the 11-party combine, while other parties could stay with their respective alliances. No party would be required to leave its alliance as a condition for participating in the initiative.

Sources at the meeting said Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis and Bangladesh Nezam-e-Islam Party had objected to imposing such conditions and believed further discussions were needed.

IDEOLOGICAL DIFFERENCE

AKM Waresul Karim, professor in the Department of Accounting and Finance and dean of the School of Business and Economics at North South University, said historical and ideological differences between Qawmi-based parties and Jamaat were part of the backdrop to the initiative.

Many Qawmi-based parties do not consider Jamaat a legitimate Islamic party, while its aqidah (creed) and religious positions have also been sources of debate among them, he said.

Therefore, he was not surprised by the move to unite separately.

Prof Waresul said although the initiative might not have a major independent political agenda, its indirect effects could ease pressure on the government. He also did not rule out possible government patronage.

A strong alliance of Qawmi-based parties, if sustained until the local body polls, could affect the Jamaat-led alliance, he said. Jamaat, National Citizen Party, and Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis are key forces within the alliance, and the departure of any of them or their leaders could weaken it.
summary: The initiative to unite seven Islamist political parties under the guidance of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh, a Qawmi madrasa-based organisation, could be a ploy to weaken political rivals, Jamaat-e-Islami Assistant Secretary General Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair has alleged.
author: Mamunur Rashid

title: Jamaat warns against election manipulation, alleges politicisation of administration
body:
Jamaat-e-Islami Assistant Secretary General Hamidur Rahman Azad today warned the government against manipulating the October 29 by-election to Thakurgaon-1, citing the 1994 Magura by-election as a cautionary example of how an election controversy can trigger a movement to oust a government.

Speaking to journalists after a meeting of the 11-party alliance’s liaison committee at the opposition leader’s official residence on Minto Road in Dhaka today, he alleged that preparations were underway to manipulate the by-election in the same way as the February 12 national election.

“If the government does not want to stay in power, we cannot force it to remain in power,” said the alliance’s liaison committee coordinator.

He said support was growing for the alliance’s candidate, Delawar Hossain, in Thakurgaon, with voters preparing to cast their ballots. Warning against a repeat of the Magura controversy, he urged the government to abandon any plan to rig the by-election.

“The Magura election was a dark chapter in the history of elections in Bangladesh. The movement to oust the government began over that election and eventually reached its climax,” he said.

At the briefing, Hamidur Rahman outlined the alliance’s demands, including implementation of the referendum verdict, trials over the July massacre, resolution of electricity, fuel, gas and fertiliser shortages, control of rising prices, an end to corruption and extortion, and improvements in law and order.

Accusing the government of politicising the administration, he alleged that appointments and promotions were being made on political grounds. He also claimed that members of the Public Service Commission (PSC) were being forced to resign after being invited to tea. He cited the appointment of Shamsul Alam to a post equivalent to additional secretary at the Election Commission as an example of politicisation.

He further alleged that the current government was following a path similar to that of the previous fascist regime, saying the expectations raised by the anti-discrimination movement were going unmet because appointments and promotions were not based on merit.

Hamidur said the alliance’s October 31 long march from Dhaka towards Khulna and Kushtia would be peaceful and orderly. He said the government and administration were responsible for ensuring participants’ safety and urged the authorities to take preventive measures against any attempt to create disorder. Otherwise, he said, the alliance would assume the administration was being used to foment chaos.

According to the organisers, the long march will begin with a rally at 7:00am on October 31 at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque in Dhaka. Opposition Leader and Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman will address the rally as chief guest.

The march will start at 8:00am with a convoy of around 1,000 vehicles. Participants are expected to pass through several districts before joining the concluding rally at Kushtia Zila School ground.
summary: 11-party alliance to march towards Khulna, Kushtia on October 31

title: Rape case plaintiff among 21 sued over madrasa looting, vandalism in Savar
body:
A case has been filed against 21 people, including the complainant in a case accusing a madrasa headteacher and owner in Savar of raping a 13-year-old student, over allegations of looting and vandalism at the institution.
